a46.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a46.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a46.title: WHO Director-General
a46.speech: Cautioned at a press conference: "The disruptions to HIV programs could undo 20 years of progress." Warned that this setback could lead to over 10 million new HIV cases and three million HIV-related deaths. Stressed: "The United States has a responsibility to ensure that if it withdraws funding, it does so in an orderly and humane way that allows affected countries to find alternative resources."

a46.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a46.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a46.speech: Warned of severe consequences in Afghanistan: as of March 4, 167 health facilities had shut down due to funding shortages, and over 220 more could close by June without urgent intervention; estimated 80% of its supported essential healthcare services in Afghanistan are at risk.

a249.speaker: The Imam of the great prayer mosque of Tahoua (sermon)
a249.name: The Imam of the great prayer mosque of Tahoua (sermon)
a249.speech: Delivered his sermon, in which he addressed the importance of sacrifice during this festival, but also dealt with unity and mutual assistance among Muslims; listed the various animals for the sacrifice, namely the ram and/or ewe, the billy goat and/or she-goat, the bull and/or cow, the male camel and/or she-camel, all of which must be in good health; said that the meat must be shared in three parts among family, friends and the needy; then prayed for peace and prosperity in Niger.

a249.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of the Tahoua region
a249.name: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé
a249.title: Governor of the Tahoua region
a249.speech: Expressed his delight at the celebration of this festival and asked the ulema to continue praying for peace and stability in the country.

a249.speaker: Mahamane Elhadj Ousmane, Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a249.name: Mahamane Elhadj Ousmane
a249.title: Minister of Agriculture and Livestock
a249.speech: Also presented his best wishes for a happy feast to all the populations of the country, and expressed the wish that this festival might bring happiness, peace and communion among the country's different communities; he also prayed for a fruitful rainy season in the country ; "I have been visiting the Tahoua region for a few days; we have seen the resilience of the population. We ask them to forgive one another, to unite in order to succeed in this noble struggle for the refoundation of Niger."

a249.speaker: Sahabi Moussa, Delegated Administrator of the city of Tahoua, and the Chief of the Canton of Tahoua
a249.name: Sahabi Moussa
a249.title: Delegated Administrator of the city of Tahoua, and the Chief of the Canton of Tahoua
a249.speech: Each in turn took the floor to present their best wishes for a happy feast and to ask forgiveness from the population of the city of Tahoua.

a249.speaker: Regional authorities present at the prayer
a249.name: Regional authorities present at the prayer
a249.speech: Presented their best wishes for a happy feast to the population.

a250.speaker: Amir Ali, US district judge (Washington)
a250.name: Amir Ali
a250.title: US district judge (Washington)
a250.speech: Noted in the order that the Government had argued it needed to freeze funding of thousands of USAID aid programmes abroad in order to conduct a full review of each programme and of whether they should be eliminated ; said Government officials "offered no explanation" as to why the suspension of all foreign aid, "which set off a shockwave and brought down" contracts with thousands of non-profit groups, companies and others, "was a rational precursor to the review of programmes."

a250.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a250.name: Donald Trump
a250.title: US President
a250.speech: Classified much of US aid as misaligned with his agenda.

a250.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State and acting director of USAID
a250.name: Marco Rubio
a250.title: US Secretary of State and acting director of USAID
a250.speech: Accused USAID of being "completely devoid of responsiveness", criticising what he described as insubordination within that body.

a250.speaker: Carl Nichols, US district judge
a250.name: Carl Nichols
a250.title: US district judge
a250.speech: Ordered the extension of the suspension of Trump's order to withdraw the overwhelming majority of USAID staff posted around the world, after a hearing of almost three hours on Thursday.

a250.speaker: USAID staff posted in the Democratic Republic of Congo
a250.name: USAID staff posted in the Democratic Republic of Congo
a250.speech: Said that the agency practically abandoned them when looting and political violence erupted in the east of that African country in January, forcing them to flee with their families.

a282.speaker: Kalidbomba (Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Agency)
a282.name: Kalidbomba (Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Agency)
a282.speech: "Even if nutrition is a clear human health issue it also has a direct relationship with the farmers and the agriculture directly." ; "The success of the hotline in this short period of time is derived by the high demand of the farmers to access helpful information."

a282.speaker: Ekin Ogutogullari, Country Director of Save the Children in Ethiopia
a282.name: Ekin Ogutogullari
a282.title: Country Director of Save the Children in Ethiopia
a282.speech: "It is a smart and timely information dissemination tool which is enabled by this partnership with ATA." ; "It helps us avoid duplication of efforts and wisely use available resources and it will contribute to the dietary consumption behavior improvement of farmers."

a282.speaker: Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Agency (ATA) and Save the Children in Ethiopia (Memorandum of Understanding)
a282.name: Ethiopian Agricultural Transformation Agency (ATA) and Save the Children in Ethiopia (Memorandum of Understanding)
a282.speech: Signed a Memorandum of Understanding to use the 8028 Farmers' Hotline to deliver nutrition-sensitive agricultural messages, agreeing to utilize Interactive Voice Response/Short Message Service (IVR/SMS) to give farmers advice on nutrition-sensitive agriculture.

a586.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (press statement sent to the newsroom)
a586.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (press statement sent to the newsroom)
a586.speech: According to a statement sent to our newsroom, the signing of the Financing Agreement between the Governments of Mozambique and the United States, through the MCC, is scheduled for September this year in Washington DC.

a616.speaker: Inspector Getu Geremew, candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation and Deputy CEO of the Ethiopian Electric Utility
a616.name: Inspector Getu Geremew
a616.title: candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation and Deputy CEO of the Ethiopian Electric Utility
a616.speech: Says that as an Ethiopian who loves the sport it astonishes and pains him that the federation is now and then a source of dispute, because athletics is not only a signature expression of Ethiopian diplomacy but a symbol of victory and a major investment option ; says that if given the opportunity he is ready to modernise the institution, noting that as deputy board chairman of the athletics, football and tennis clubs under the Ethiopian Electric Utility he has worked with colleagues to reform all three clubs, and that his two decades of supporting athletics are the basis for his candidacy.

a616.speaker: Inspector Getu Geremew, candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.name: Inspector Getu Geremew
a616.title: candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.speech: Says that what the institution lacks is leadership quality, noting that from Rio to the Paris Olympics there were athletes capable of winning three or more gold medals but results disappeared because they could not be coordinated ; says he does not believe the institution can be led merely because someone ran or knows the science of running ; says he is coming to be part of the solution through open and participatory discussions with stakeholders and by preparing systems and directives, and that if selection criteria everyone agrees on were drawn up six months or more before the election, the current arguments and squabbles could not exist.

a616.speaker: Inspector Getu Geremew, candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.name: Inspector Getu Geremew
a616.title: candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.speech: Says the laws stipulate that sport is free from ethnicity, gender, culture, neighbourhood, language and race, and that the solution on the question of foreign currency and managers requires identifying and formulating the division of responsibilities ; says managers who work respecting rules in Kenya and similar countries give him no reason to expect different behaviour in Ethiopia, and that in his time managers will have to build camps and academies or face difficulty ; says it is surprising that Ethiopia has never had a single representative in international sports institutions, which he personally feels comes from a leadership gap, and that his aim is to enable Ethiopia to obtain the place it deserves at World Athletics level, including in diplomacy.

a616.speaker: Inspector Getu Geremew, candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.name: Inspector Getu Geremew
a616.title: candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.speech: Says the matter of the national team is the foremost of the fundamentals enabling Ethiopia to shine on international sports stages and that a scattered team has no capacity, citing the national team of Dr Woldemeskel Kostre's era whose team spirit alone made athletes winners ; says that if asked the reason for the current decline it is, without hesitation, the dissolution or scattering of the national team, which he sees as a big gap ; says "Restoring the spirit of cooperation and unity that has been lost in athletics will be my main area of work."

a616.speaker: Inspector Getu Geremew, candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.name: Inspector Getu Geremew
a616.title: candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.speech: Says the coaches' certification issue needs to be looked at in three parts, because placing the professional at the grade that befits him is decisive, and that after a coach's certification is determined it must be implemented by correctly distinguishing between youth, junior and senior teams - work he lists among his main plans ; says the procedure must also be clearly formulated because disputes have arisen over who did what in connection with foreign travel, since a person who has worked must get the value of his effort.

a616.speaker: Inspector Getu Geremew, candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.name: Inspector Getu Geremew
a616.title: candidate for President of the Ethiopian Athletics Federation
a616.speech: Says it is naive to think Ethiopia can succeed with the old approach and training methods, since results today require research, nutrition, training venues and coaching, and that better training facilities must of necessity be built or athletics will pay a price ; says small community-owned training facilities should be built, that Ethiopian Airlines, Ethio Telecom and his own institution should be persuaded to support and own the sport, that work with equipment manufacturers such as Adidas and Nike and with managers is needed on tracks, that he is starting work to lay a track in the Gofa Electric Power area, and that he will work to bring veteran athletes closer to the institution to share their advice and experience.

a830.speaker: US Government, led by Donald Trump
a830.name: US Government
a830.title: led by Donald Trump
a830.speech: Announced last night the end of the operations of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), created in 1961 and considered for decades the world’s largest distributor of humanitarian aid; it was announced during the closure process that, of the roughly 10,000 employees and contractors of the agency in Washington and its offices around the world, only 294 would remain to maintain minimum operations.

a830.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (statement, cited by RTP)
a830.name: Marco Rubio
a830.title: US Secretary of State (statement, cited by RTP)
a830.speech: Stressed in a statement that USAID had not fulfilled its objectives since the end of the Cold War and had created a network of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) that lived “at the expense of American taxpayers”: “This era of inefficiency has officially come to an end. Under the Trump administration, we will finally have foreign aid that prioritises our national interests” ; said American citizens “should not pay taxes to finance bankrupt governments in distant countries” and promised that from now on “aid will be targeted and limited in time”.

a830.speaker: Humanitarian aid experts and international organisations
a830.name: Humanitarian aid experts and international organisations
a830.speech: Heavily criticised the end of USAID, warning that its disappearance leaves an enormous gap in health, education and humanitarian crisis response programmes.

a830.speaker: Barack Obama and George W. Bush, former US presidents
a830.name: Barack Obama and George W. Bush
a830.title: former US presidents
a830.speech: Directed rare criticism at the Trump government on Monday.

a830.speaker: Bono, singer
a830.name: Bono
a830.title: singer
a830.speech: Became emotional as he recited a poem at a farewell event for the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

a830.speaker: Study coordinated by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal), published in The Lancet
a830.name: Study coordinated by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal)
a830.title: published in The Lancet
a830.speech: Warned that the cuts to American aid could lead to more than 14 million ‘preventable’ deaths by 2030; according to the study, USAID had a fundamental impact in reducing mortality from HIV/AIDS, malaria and neglected tropical diseases worldwide.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué of the 8th summit, Brazzaville, 30 January 2020)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué of the 8th summit
a838.title: Brazzaville, 30 January 2020)
a838.speech: The members of the Committee expressed their deep concern at the deterioration of the security, humanitarian and economic situation in Libya, making living conditions for the population increasingly difficult, and noted that this situation feeds terrorist, criminal and human-trafficking networks that destabilise several countries of the sub-region.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Reaffirmed its solidarity with the Libyan people and its firm attachment to the country's territorial integrity, national unity and independence ; Took note of Algeria's offer to bring the different views closer together and reiterated its commitment to promoting a return to negotiations in line with earlier African Union decisions on reconciliation in Libya, recalling the earlier decision of the Assembly of Heads of State to organise an inter-Libyan national reconciliation forum in Addis Ababa.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Appreciated the efforts of Libya's neighbouring countries and the sacrifices made to assist Libyan populations affected by the crisis, and called for these efforts to continue in accordance with the decisions of the Assembly of Heads of State and Government.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Committed itself to the Libyan political dialogue, recalling the urgency of an inclusive dialogue bringing together all Libyan parties to promote an end to the conflict and the search for a Libyan solution to the crisis, taking into account the higher interests of the Libyan people.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Firmly condemned the continuation of fighting in the capital Tripoli and its surroundings and reiterated the urgency of a complete and effective ceasefire accompanied by a monitoring mechanism in which the African Union would be involved ; Called on African Union member states to deploy military observers, once conditions are met, to take part in the ceasefire monitoring mechanism and to liaise with the Libyan parties.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Condemned the continuation of external interference in Libya in the wake of the commitments made in Berlin and renewed its call on all external actors to cease immediately all interference in Libya's internal affairs, notably the delivery of weapons and the recruitment of mercenaries, which exacerbate the crisis with consequences for people's lives and threaten the fundamental interests of the Libyan people and their legitimate aspirations to freedom, peace, democracy and development.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Insisted on strict respect for the arms embargo decreed by the Security Council on Libya and called on the Security Council to apply the sanctions provided for in the event of violation.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Energetically condemned terrorist activities, the use of foreign fighters and recourse to mercenaries, as well as any facilitation of illegal transit, transport or recruitment in violation of the OAU Convention on the Elimination of Mercenarism in Africa of 3 July 1977.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Expressed its concern at the unprecedented level of circulation of sophisticated weapons in Libya, which aggravates the conflict and threatens the peace and security of the country, of neighbouring States and of the Sahel ; Called on the African Union Commission to ensure the implementation by member states of mechanisms to combat cross-border crime and terrorism.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Deeply concerned by the deterioration of the humanitarian situation in Libya, called for international protection of African migrants detained and held in Libya and used as fighters and human shields, and for facilitation of their repatriation to their countries of origin.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Called for the mobilisation of humanitarian aid for vulnerable populations, refugees and internally displaced persons, and called on the warring parties to ensure strict respect for International Humanitarian Law, notably by securing hospitals and schools and facilitating the delivery of aid.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Underlined the principle of the permanent sovereignty of peoples over their natural resources and reaffirmed that these are the property of the Libyan people, and therefore called for the reopening of the oil terminals so that the Libyan people can fully benefit from their resources ; Recalled that civilian port and airport facilities must be put at the service of Libyan citizens and kept outside any military activity that endangers civilians' lives or prevents them from benefiting from the services of those facilities.

a838.speaker: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.name: African Union High-Level Committee on Libya (final communiqué)
a838.speech: Decided to prepare and hold the inter-Libyan Reconciliation Conference in accordance with the relevant African Union decisions, in consultation with neighbouring countries and the United Nations ; Decided to create an Inclusive Preparatory Commission for the conference, open to all Libyan stakeholders including tribal chiefs, women, young people and other political and social forces, to promote a lasting solution to the conflict ; Adopted a Roadmap setting out the main stages of the process, deciding on the creation of the forum's preparatory commission, the calendar of its meetings, and the human and financial resources required for the success of its mission.

a872.speaker: Brian Shukan, United States Ambassador to Benin
a872.name: Brian Shukan
a872.title: United States Ambassador to Benin
a872.speech: Welcomed the entry into service of the facility, the fruit of cooperation between Benin and the United States: “MCA-Benin II is the best symbol of the cooperation between Benin and the United States, which has lasted for 60 years.”

a872.speaker: Gabriel Dégbègni, National Coordinator of MCA-Benin II
a872.name: Gabriel Dégbègni
a872.title: National Coordinator of MCA-Benin II
a872.speech: Says he is proud to take stock of the new infrastructure the country is benefiting from: “It is a source of pride for the staff of MCA-Benin II, who overcame a good number of challenges to achieve the objectives.”

a872.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State in charge of Development and Coordination of Government Action and Chairman of the Board of MCA-Benin II
a872.name: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané
a872.title: Minister of State in charge of Development and Coordination of Government Action and Chairman of the Board of MCA-Benin II
a872.speech: Welcomed the implementation of MCA-Benin II, which impacts 12 million Beninese and opens prospects for Benin’s economic development thanks to the availability of electricity: “The Compact is the best development financing tool.”

a1053.speaker: Monica Mutsvangwa, Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.name: Monica Mutsvangwa
a1053.title: Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.speech: Said on Friday, while opening a four-day MSME training manual validation workshop in Bulawayo, that the Zimbabwe government recognises the vital role that Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play in driving economic growth, job creation, and sustainable development: "MSMEs contribute significantly to value addition, exports growth, and providing essential ancillary services across sectors." ; "Therefore, government recognises the substantial role played by MSMEs in driving economic growth and sustainable development in Zimbabwe through creating jobs, providing key ancillary services in almost all sectors of the economy, driving value addition and export growth."

a1053.speaker: Monica Mutsvangwa, Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.name: Monica Mutsvangwa
a1053.title: Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.speech: Highlighted that the MSME sector employs 4.8 million people on a full-time basis and contributes more than 60% to the country's Gross Domestic Product, and acknowledged several challenges the sector faces, including limited access to finance, markets, appropriate workspaces, and insufficient business management skills: "Furthermore, it must be noted that the business environment is marked by uncertainty, economic shocks, and rapid changes." ; "There is therefore a need for robust and coordinated supportive mechanisms by all stakeholders to build the capacity of SMEs to survive in this environment."

a1053.speaker: 2021 MSMEs Survey
a1053.name: 2021 MSMEs Survey
a1053.speech: Cited as the source for the finding that the MSME sector employs 4.8 million people on a full-time basis and contributes more than 60% to the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

a1053.speaker: Monica Mutsvangwa, Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.name: Monica Mutsvangwa
a1053.title: Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.speech: Said her ministry remains committed to providing MSMEs with resources, training, and opportunities to unlock their potential: "Guided by the MSMEs Policy Framework (2020-2024), the Ministry is implementing a number of programs meant to address these challenges." ; "These initiatives include funding through the Women Development Fund (WDF), Community Development Fund (CDF), Zimbabwe Women Microfinance Bank (ZWMB), and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Corporation (SMEDCO), construction of MSMEs factory shells to ensure MSMEs have decent workspaces, business management skills training, assisting MSMEs to exhibit their products and services at various exhibitions and expos locally and internationally, among others."

a1053.speaker: Monica Mutsvangwa, Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.name: Monica Mutsvangwa
a1053.title: Zimbabwe Minister of Women Affairs, Community, and Small and Medium Enterprises Development
a1053.speech: Commended UNDESA for supporting the development of the manual, saying it will positively enhance the capacity of MSMEs to manage and grow their businesses in a highly competitive business environment, and emphasised the importance of sustainable risk management practices for MSMEs, citing the recent fire at the Mbare Traders' Market, where traders lost millions worth of goods.

a1140.speaker: Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL)
a1140.name: Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL)
a1140.speech: Calls for the protection of female journalists in Liberia and is calling for a safe working environment for women journalists across Liberia as the world commemorates 16 Days of Activism to end all forms of violence against women and girls.

a1140.speaker: Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL) (press statement)
a1140.name: Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL) (press statement)
a1140.speech: Says it will utilize the media through advocacy, talkshows and social media campaigns to raise public awareness on the need to protect rights of women journalists in Liberia. In a press statement, FeJAL says these discussions will focus on critical topics such as challenges faced by women journalists in the newsroom, promoting safe workspaces, protecting their rights, and supporting women's leadership in the media.

a1140.speaker: Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL)
a1140.name: Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL)
a1140.speech: Says it aims to mobilize media stakeholders, change dynamics on promoting a workspace free of intimidation, harassment and exploitation of women in the media during these 16 days of activism, and believes that through collective action and collaboration, concrete steps can be taken to create lasting change for the betterment of women journalists in Liberia.

a1146.speaker: Guy Lavender, Chief Executive & Secretary of MCC
a1146.name: Guy Lavender
a1146.title: Chief Executive & Secretary of MCC
a1146.speech: "We are thrilled to be able to announce our newest cohort of Honorary Life Members of MCC as we prepare for the new international summer. The names that have been announced today are some of the greatest international players of modern times, and we are privileged to now count them as valued Members of our Club. We are also pleased to be able to announce two individuals who have been awarded this honour for their monumental contributions off the pitch."

a1225.speaker: Simon Namesho, University of Namibia (Unam) spokesperson
a1225.name: Simon Namesho
a1225.title: University of Namibia (Unam) spokesperson
a1225.speech: said “This year, however, the numbers notably increased, reflecting a transformative shift in public perception and engagement,” adding that extensive media coverage and public discussions early in 2025 had spurred people’s interest.

a1225.speaker: Dr Anneli Poolman, senior lecturer in anatomy, University of Namibia
a1225.name: Dr Anneli Poolman
a1225.title: senior lecturer in anatomy, University of Namibia
a1225.speech: emphasised the importance of the rising trend: “Each pledge significantly enriches the practical education of our future medical professionals. The increase in public interest is truly encouraging, supporting a greater understanding of how vital these donations are for medical training,” adding that from comparing numbers, the rise in interest is strikingly evident ; said this clearly proves a significant shift in public engagement and willingness to support medical education.

a1225.speaker: Dr Anneli Poolman, senior lecturer in anatomy, University of Namibia
a1225.name: Dr Anneli Poolman
a1225.title: senior lecturer in anatomy, University of Namibia
a1225.speech: said Namibian body donations eliminate the complex, expensive logistical challenges associated with international transportation and embalming, as opposed to relying on costly imports from countries such as South Africa.

a1225.speaker: University of Namibia
a1225.name: University of Namibia
a1225.speech: noted that the practical implications of receiving Namibian donors, as opposed to relying on costly imports from countries such as South Africa, are profound.

a1225.speaker: Professor Judith Hall, Executive Dean of the Faculty of Health Sciences and Veterinary Medicine, University of Namibia
a1225.name: Professor Judith Hall
a1225.title: Executive Dean of the Faculty of Health Sciences and Veterinary Medicine, University of Namibia
a1225.speech: remarked: “Local body donations symbolise community support for Namibia’s healthcare education system. It’s a powerful statement of national pride and unity.”

a1225.speaker: Dr Felicia Christians, Associate Dean of the School of Medicine, University of Namibia
a1225.name: Dr Felicia Christians
a1225.title: Associate Dean of the School of Medicine, University of Namibia
a1225.speech: noted: “The recent rise in body donation pledges reflects greater openness and acceptance among Namibians. It’s a commendable act, showing a progressive mindset towards supporting medical research and education in Namibia.”

a1246.speaker: European Union
a1246.name: European Union
a1246.speech: Said it is releasing an additional €250,000 (over N450 million) in humanitarian assistance to help people in need in response to the mass displacement caused by a series of violent attacks by armed groups across Benue and Plateau States of Nigeria ; said that the funding will enable the Nigerian Red Cross to deliver immediate, life-saving humanitarian assistance to 2,500 vulnerable households (around 15,000 people) who have been displaced over four months, including emergency cash assistance, essential household items, healthcare and psychosocial support, as well as water and sanitation ; said in July that it provided the International Organization for Migration (IOM) with €500,000 (approximately NGN 886,315,000) to meet the most urgent needs of displaced populations in Benue state for a period of 6 months.

a1246.speaker: European Union (statement)
a1246.name: European Union (statement)
a1246.speech: Noted that beyond immediate relief, the initiative will strengthen protection services and conduct awareness campaigns on health, hygiene, and safety: “This comprehensive approach aims to not only alleviate suffering but also to safeguard the dignity of vulnerable people—especially women, children, and those repeatedly displaced—who are now living in precarious, overcrowded, and underserved conditions.” ; noted that many are subsistence farmers cut off from their land during the crucial planting season and that the majority reside in overcrowded internally displaced people camps or informal shelters, facing severe shortages of food, clean water, healthcare, and protection ; “The recurring and targeted violence in Benue and Plateau States continues to fuel a protracted protection crisis, leading to widespread destruction and a deepening humanitarian emergency. With new security threats emerging weekly, the need for sustained humanitarian action remains paramount.”

a1329.speaker: Cristódia, teacher
a1329.name: Cristódia
a1329.title: teacher
a1329.speech: "With the support that parents and guardians have been giving for the construction of classrooms, I wanted to ask the Government, at least for the schools that already exist, to support them with desks, because the children come out of the shade [of outdoor classes] but return to classrooms to sit on the floor."

a1329.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique (Head of State)
a1329.name: Daniel Chapo
a1329.title: President of the Republic of Mozambique (Head of State)
a1329.speech: In response to this question, praised the participation of communities in the construction of classrooms and reiterated the need for other measures to equip the classrooms.

a1329.speaker: Public servants and State employees of Maputo Province
a1329.name: Public servants and State employees of Maputo Province
a1329.speech: Raised various social issues of concern, including the lack of security in schools and the closure of the USAID offices in Maputo, and put forward suggestions for the executive ; complained about the absence of protection police in schools, owing to an alleged lack of personnel ; showed themselves to be concerned about USAID's departure from the country, particularly with regard to the supply of medicines to people with HIV: "I wanted to ask the Government here to find measures so that the Mozambican people can urgently find solutions so that there are HIV/AIDS response activities at the national level."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: Said the issue of his resignation had nothing to do with the President of Liberia asking him to step down: "The whole scenario started on a false premise. The president did not ask me resign. There was no negative reaction between the president and me. When Stanton Witherspoon was putting it out there that the president was going to sack me, it was a lie. The president and I did speak. He gave me the encouragement that he understood the lot of pressure I was enduring." ; "I was called to the Legislature almost three times a week... sometimes I felt that I was being harassed. And it was distracting me from my core responsibilities... I don't own the Ministry of Commerce. I don't own the position as minister... it was a personal decision." ; "My decision to resign was based on three main reasons... people called me a foreigner; there was lot of mixed signals. There was lot of questions of me assuming responsibility as the Minister of Commerce, considering my Lebanese heritage." ; "The second thing was, at that time, it was a scenario where my wife's vehicle was attacked while she was bringing my kids from school... So, my family safety was of concern." ; "I am not above the Liberian people. I am not above the law, And at that point in time the best option was to give the president the time, and the people the opportunity to hear the truth, if it meant me stepping aside, I had no problem doing it."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: Said the incident leading to his resignation was based on lies and a false premise: "The first lie was I was gifted US$150,000... Two, that I was gifted a car similar to President Biden's car, which is false. When I assumed the mantle of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, I met US$4,800 in the ministry's account... I was the first minister who painted the entire ministry. I did that out of my pocket." ; "for the eight months I served as Minister of Commerce, I used my personal vehicle, an X-Class Mercedes far more expensive than the vehicle. I fueled it, I paid my driver, not receiving a single scratch card, not receiving a single gas slip." ; "Purchase of vehicle was functional - it was an off-road vehicle for the function of the Ministry of Commerce. When I left, where is the vehicle? It is still with the government. So, the first lie is that it was a gift to me." ; "there was no transaction between me, the Ministry of Commerce and the vendor of that vehicle... LRA interacted directly with the vendor, not through the Ministry of Commerce. No money came to the Ministry of Commerce, not to Amin Modad. The paper trail is there." ; "Thirdly, the budgetary law or the premise that set the cap for the US$45,000 was not in place till June. We started the purchase of the vehicle in March. So that ceiling, that people say we broke the ceiling, it was not intentional because the budgetary ceiling was not established." ; "In hindsight, would I have bought a car for US$98,000? No, I wouldn't... But I listened to the sentiments."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: Said he believed President Boakai initiated an investigation into the vehicle purchase: "I believe there was an investigation. When I was called to meet the president on this, he arrived on Saturday, I met him on Tuesday. During that conversation, you had the Minister of State, his political advisor, security advisor. They had done some investigation. It was clear there was no corruption... The only sentiment the president conveyed to me personally was the cost of the vehicle." ; said that in 2023 he applied to IB Bank and several banking institutions to consolidate his bad debts and was approved a loan of US$1.4 million, and that on resigning he wrote the LACC and the GAC inviting them to audit him: "I had nothing to hide. These were all lies."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: Said he became targeted for misinformation campaigns because he went against the status quo: "I was doing my job, and doing your job means you were going against the status quo. There were concessions that were importing every single thing you can think about. I put a stop to that. I ensured that they purchase locally... I opened the market. You saw the reduction in price of every commodity on the market. I broadened the rice market... So, I faced pressure from the opposition, I faced pressure from some members of the business community who were not happy that I had broadened the market. I faced pressure by politicians who benefited from the status quo."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: Lamented how Liberians hid beneath the cloak of advocacy to extort him: "We have some very good advocates, but we have a very corrupt society... Even the press is very corrupt. I have records of editors/publishers calling me and sending me screenshots of Monday's newspaper release, 'The Most Corrupt Minister- Stole US$150,000'. If you don't give me US$3,000 I will publish it." ; "There is not much real advocacy in Liberia. A lot of the advocacy is exploitative. There were personal interests all along."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: Maintained he has a cozy relationship with President Joseph Nyuma Boakai: "He and I spoke about a month ago. I still believe the President has explicit confidence in me. He knows there was no corruption. He did his own investigation... My life has been open. I am still open to any investigation."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: Said of his role in the Unity Party: "I am still a full-fledged member of the Unity Party. I am leader in the Unity Party. I also serve as chairman of the National Advisory Council of the Unity Party. So there is no issue with the Unity Party. The reaction by the chairman was an issue, something that was not appreciated across the board of the Unity Party." ; criticised Chairman Tarpeh: "Your first press conference was to denigrate your predecessor. I leave it with him, I hold nothing against him." ; "What I expected from him as chairman, and from anybody who had doubt in my credibility, the most professional and appropriate thing to do was to call me or to investigate."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: On the Boakai administration's impact and the withdrawal of US aid: "The government is already making positive impact. Road projects are going on... Road projects have picked off, the health system is being revamped, electricity, water, telecommunications, all the basic ingredients to have a functional society and economy are improving." ; "But there are also challenges... Let's look at USAID, the cessation of support to Liberia and globally. USAID was investing into Liberia US$200 million annually with their various social programs in healthcare, education. Those were providing indirect support to the budget by donor support. Those troubles are not going away. It is the government obligation now to find means to support those areas. I heard the other day that there was a shortage of HIV medication. A lot of that came from the donor support. There are a lot of existential issues that are impacting our economy, our society that the government is addressing responsibly." ; "We are vying for seat at the Security Council. I just learned that the Minister of Finance has been elected in a global body. The Minister of Health was elected as Vice Chair of a global health group. We are making progress."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: On Senator Snowe's "government failure" statement: "I did not question a lot of things Senator Snowe said. Everyone has the right to criticize government... But when you say you wish the government to fail, I take exception to it... If the government fails, you fail as a senator or as a representative." ; "Honorable Snowe was one of those that went on Spoon TV to perpetuate this malicious story about me and this vehicle... It was after he and Senator McGill went out with this malicious story, that's when my wife and kids were attacked." ; "Snowe is someone we all know is only concerned about himself, politically... He just needs to apologize."

a1367.speaker: Amin Modad, former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.name: Amin Modad
a1367.title: former Liberian Minister of Commerce and Industry
a1367.speech: On a possible CDC comeback: "They made their decision to change the CDC based on its performance. Where we are right now, I believe fervently the Unity Party is performing. I think by 2027 we will see more profound impact on the economy. People lives are changing already. There is a semblance of international credibility. The business community has credibility in the government. There is progress despite the challenges. I am not saying that CDC doesn't have a political space, but with the performance that the Unity Party has started, and I know it will continue, Unity Party will be re-elected."

a1367.speaker: Stanton Witherspoon, Liberian media commentator (Spoon TV)
a1367.name: Stanton Witherspoon
a1367.title: Liberian media commentator (Spoon TV)
a1367.speech: "was putting it out there that the president was going to sack me" - claims Modad said were a lie, including the narrative that Modad was renovating his hotel only after becoming minister.

a1367.speaker: Nathaniel McGill, Liberian Senator
a1367.name: Nathaniel McGill
a1367.title: Liberian Senator
a1367.speech: "went out and said I bought a yacht similar to a yacht owned by President Tubman", according to Modad, who called the claim outrageous.

a1367.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a1367.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a1367.title: President of Liberia
a1367.speech: Asked Modad, according to Modad's account: "for US$98,000 is that the cheapest you could have gotten?"

a1367.speaker: Liberian Legislature (confirmation hearing)
a1367.name: Liberian Legislature (confirmation hearing)
a1367.speech: Asked Modad at his hearing: "if you are not getting results, if you are not making impact, will you resign?"

a1367.speaker: Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA)
a1367.name: Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA)
a1367.speech: "responded out of the three vehicles that we requested for, that they would provide support for two of them - one for up to US$100,000, and one for US$33,000", and clarified that it did provide certain vehicles for the Ministry of Commerce, though not the quantity that had been reported.

a1367.speaker: Joseph Snowe (Bomi County Senator)
a1367.name: Joseph Snowe (Bomi County Senator)
a1367.speech: Made a statement in which he wished that the Boakai government fails because he, as a major opposition player, wants the Unity Party government to be a one-term administration; he also complained about his safety.

a1441.speaker: Fathi Bashe, YLP alumnus and youth activist
a1441.name: Fathi Bashe
a1441.title: YLP alumnus and youth activist
a1441.speech: stresses the importance of collective roles and responsibilities in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals; shared with the young Djiboutians of the YLP6 programme his experiences and his commitment to realising the Sustainable Development Goals in the Horn of Africa region.

a1441.speaker: Fatima Elsheikh, UNDP Resident Representative in Djibouti
a1441.name: Fatima Elsheikh
a1441.title: UNDP Resident Representative in Djibouti
a1441.speech: congratulated the young people taking part in YLP6 this year for their commitment and diligence and their genuine leadership, which is very promising.

a1441.speaker: Officials present at the ceremony
a1441.name: Officials present at the ceremony
a1441.speech: welcomed this programme, which involves young people and allows them to exchange experiences, enrich one another and compare their ideas. "It is not only a matter of working for young people but of working with young people," they insisted.

a1448.speaker: Terence Musuku, Zambia Boxing Federation (ZBF) life member
a1448.name: Terence Musuku
a1448.title: Zambia Boxing Federation (ZBF) life member
a1448.speech: has called on the newly-elected executive led by Boniface Sokoni to utilise his vast knowledge to steer the sport.

a1448.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a1448.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a1448.title: President of Zambia
a1448.speech: says suspension of United States Agency for International Development (USAID) programmes globally by the Trump administration is long overdue.

a1448.speaker: Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency (ZAMMSA)
a1448.name: Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency (ZAMMSA)
a1448.speech: has assured of an uninterrupted supply of medicines countrywide as Government has a well-defined plan of buying drugs.

a1487.speaker: International Labour Organization (ILO)
a1487.name: International Labour Organization (ILO)
a1487.speech: According to the ILO, at least 61% of jobs have been lost in the Gaza Strip since the start of the fighting between Israel and Hamas; the West Bank is also affected with a loss of about 24% of jobs, and the shortfall in daily income for the Occupied Palestinian Territories is estimated at 16 million dollars.

a1487.speaker: ILO bulletin “The impact of the Israel-Hamas conflict on the labour market and on livelihoods in the occupied Palestinian territory” (published 6 November)
a1487.name: ILO bulletin “The impact of the Israel-Hamas conflict on the labour market and on livelihoods in the occupied Palestinian territory” (published 6 November)
a1487.speech: States that the total number of jobs lost in the two areas (Gaza and the West Bank) making up the Occupied Palestinian Territories is estimated at 390,000, translating into daily labour income losses of 16 million dollars; at least 182,000 jobs (61%) have been lost in the Gaza Strip and 208,000 jobs (24%) in the West Bank over the period 7 to 31 October 2023. The publication indicates that the conflict has serious repercussions not only on the labour market and employment prospects but also on livelihoods across the Occupied Palestinian Territories. The bulletin stresses that entire neighbourhoods of Gaza have been destroyed, infrastructure severely damaged, businesses closed, large-scale internal displacement has occurred, and the lack of water, food and fuel is paralysing economic activity.

a1487.speaker: ILO labour force survey, second quarter of 2023
a1487.name: ILO labour force survey
a1487.title: second quarter of 2023
a1487.speech: Found that the unemployment rate in Gaza reached 46.4% (66.2% for women and 40.5% for men).

a1487.speaker: Ruba Jaradat, ILO Regional Director for Arab States
a1487.name: Ruba Jaradat
a1487.title: ILO Regional Director for Arab States
a1487.speech: Declared that “the ongoing hostilities do not only represent an enormous humanitarian crisis in terms of loss of human life and basic human needs, they also represent a social and economic crisis that has caused enormous damage to jobs and businesses, with repercussions that will be felt for many years to come.” ; Ruba Jaradat specified that in the long term the ILO would help workers “to recover jobs by linking them to social protection initiatives, to the fullest extent of our mandate.”

a1487.speaker: ILO Governing Body
a1487.name: ILO Governing Body
a1487.speech: Launched an appeal, in accordance with international humanitarian law, for rapid and safe humanitarian access to allow the delivery of humanitarian aid to civilians throughout the Gaza Strip.

a1586.speaker: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a1586.name: Economics Association of Malawi (Ecama)
a1586.speech: has warned that Reserve Bank of Malawi's (RBM) over-reliance on policy rate hikes to curb inflation cannot be sufficient without complementary structural and fiscal reforms to boost production.

a1586.speaker: Esmie Kanyumbu, Ecama executive director
a1586.name: Esmie Kanyumbu
a1586.title: Ecama executive director
a1586.speech: told the Monetary Policy Technical Forum in Lilongwe that the RBM should also direct efforts towards supporting the real economy and improving institutional transparency ; "Aside from using the policy rate, the central bank should prioritise efforts to ensure that there is financing to the real economy."

a1586.speaker: Esmie Kanyumbu, Ecama executive director
a1586.name: Esmie Kanyumbu
a1586.title: Ecama executive director
a1586.speech: questioned the reliability of RBM's inflation projections, citing the likelihood of persistent structural risks as the country moves closer to the September 16 General Election ; "Maize prices are expected to remain high in 2025 and fiscal pressures are likely to intensify as we approach the polls. The projections appear somewhat optimistic considering these structural risks."

a1586.speaker: Esmie Kanyumbu, Ecama executive director
a1586.name: Esmie Kanyumbu
a1586.title: Ecama executive director
a1586.speech: raised concerns over transparency in foreign exchange management, stating that the lack of accurate and timely data on foreign exchange reserves could undermine investor confidence.

a1586.speaker: National Statistical Office
a1586.name: National Statistical Office
a1586.speech: Inflation rate stood at 30.5 percent as of March 2025, according to the National Statistical Office.

a1586.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a1586.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a1586.speech: forecasts that inflation is expected to average 27 percent this year from 32.2 percent last year ; remains cautiously optimistic, projecting that economic growth will rebound to 3.2 percent in 2025 from 1.8 percent in the previous year, premised on improvements in agriculture, mining and services, conditional on stable weather and improved input distribution.

a1586.speaker: Chikumbutso Galeta, RBM manager for market analysis and development
a1586.name: Chikumbutso Galeta
a1586.title: RBM manager for market analysis and development
a1586.speech: said that while year-on-year headline inflation rate is expected to ease from 32.2 percent in 2024 to 27 percent this year, food inflation has instead edged upwards ; "At the first meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee this year, we expected prices to ease in the second quarter. But inflation is proving sticky and supply-side constraints, erratic weather and delays in key programmes such as the Affordable Inputs Programme are keeping upward pressure on prices."

a1586.speaker: Chikumbutso Galeta, RBM manager for market analysis and development
a1586.name: Chikumbutso Galeta
a1586.title: RBM manager for market analysis and development
a1586.speech: said what is further compounding the situation is the recent withdrawal of aid by the United States through the United States Agency for International Development, which is expected to create a significant fiscal gap that government must now absorb.

a1586.speaker: United States Department of State
a1586.name: United States Department of State
a1586.speech: The US Government was giving more than $350 million (about K612.8 billion) to Malawi annually, according to the United States Department of State.

a1586.speaker: Nico Asset Managers
a1586.name: Nico Asset Managers
a1586.speech: earlier warned that inflationary headwinds will continue to linger, arising from fiscal slippages, weak kwacha, increases in electricity tariffs and higher government expenditure due to the forthcoming September 16 General Election.

a1722.speaker: Participants of the fourth technical meeting of the CountrySTAT Technical Working Group
a1722.name: Participants of the fourth technical meeting of the CountrySTAT Technical Working Group
a1722.speech: Expressed the wish that certain bodies such as CENATEL and CENAGREF be contacted in order to obtain other information to put on the site, such as land occupation and soil mapping, forest cover and hydrography, and health data ; praised all the efforts made by the members of the secretariat so that the launch would indeed take place on Thursday 3 June 2010.

a1722.speaker: Aboudoulaye Mouphtaou, Representative of the National Food Security Office (ONASA) in the CountrySTAT Technical Working Group
a1722.name: Aboudoulaye Mouphtaou
a1722.title: Representative of the National Food Security Office (ONASA) in the CountrySTAT Technical Working Group
a1722.speech: "The establishment of CountrySTAT has been welcomed by the National Food Security Office (ONASA). The data gathered here and there will allow us to better assess the indicators for meaningful food security."

a1722.speaker: Gbodogbe Pascal, representative of the Regional Centre for Agricultural Promotion (CeRPA) Atlantique/Littoral
a1722.name: Gbodogbe Pascal
a1722.title: representative of the Regional Centre for Agricultural Promotion (CeRPA) Atlantique/Littoral
a1722.speech: "CountrySTAT being a database or a national statistical information system on a given subject, and with reference to a given structure, it turns out that CountrySTAT provides information on the primary production of food crops, the quantity of food consumption, the annual production of fish from capture fisheries in live-weight equivalent and in value, the number of boats used during the year and the number of jobs generated, the secondary sector, imports and exports, etc., which brings out the indicator of the well-being of populations in feeding, housing, clothing and educating themselves."

a1722.speaker: Agonyissa Didier, representative of CeRPA Mono/Couffo
a1722.name: Agonyissa Didier
a1722.title: representative of CeRPA Mono/Couffo
a1722.speech: "The data that CeRPA Mono/Couffo makes available to the unit concern forecasts and actual outturns in crop production, rainfall data, etc. Already, simple analysis of the results of crop production outturns can make it possible to identify the zones and the communes that specialise in the production of one crop or another." ; Said the data consulted directly on the CountrySTAT site can serve decision-making and the drawing up of projects or programmes to improve yields and increase agricultural production in Mono and Couffo; that a wholesale rice trader could use the site to identify producing zones and direct purchases, benefiting both traders and producers; that crop production and demographic data make it possible to draw up the food balance sheet and to take decisions for the lean season; and that "the importance of statistics in general and of agricultural statistics in particular no longer needs to be demonstrated. They make it possible to evaluate the actions of projects or programmes, to take major decisions at various levels (communal, regional, national, etc.), and to target areas where support to producers needs to be strengthened."

a1722.speaker: Gangbazo Hermann, representative of the Directorate of Fisheries
a1722.name: Gangbazo Hermann
a1722.title: representative of the Directorate of Fisheries
a1722.speech: "With CountrySTAT today, students in search of statistical data for research work, researchers and academics will no longer have any trouble accessing data. They will simply have to connect to the internet and access the CountrySTAT site to obtain these data." ; Said CountrySTAT will constitute an opening to the whole world, a great portal for Benin on its fishing activities with a view to attracting national and international investors; that its implementation will make it possible to diversify fishing activity, with deep-sea fishing targeted; that the FAO will no longer have to send forms to be filled in; that a would-be investor will be able to obtain all the data for a feasibility study; and that politicians will be able to initiate development projects for fishing communities.

a1722.speaker: Hounkpevi Théodore, representative of CeRPA Ouémé/Plateau
a1722.name: Hounkpevi Théodore
a1722.title: representative of CeRPA Ouémé/Plateau
a1722.speech: "CountrySTAT today fills a gap in the location of agricultural statistics in our country. It makes reliable information on agricultural production permanently available. It is easy to access and its monitoring and coordination by the FAO confer on it reliability and credibility. The FAO and the national authorities must ensure it is supported, by providing it with human and material resources for its sustainability."

a1722.speaker: Didavi Edgard, National Secretary for the Coordination of CountrySTAT Benin
a1722.name: Didavi Edgard
a1722.title: National Secretary for the Coordination of CountrySTAT Benin
a1722.speech: Said activities on CountrySTAT started in Benin in the last quarter of 2008; that three technical meetings were held in 2009 for the collection and validation of data; described the first meeting as informing members of the National Integrated Agricultural Statistics System (SNISA) of CountrySTAT's objectives and activities, the second as producing and validating some twenty tables, and the third as reformatting validated tables and preparing about ten more; and said that taking into account the observations on the tables presented at this fourth meeting "will make it possible to fulfil the expectations of the said workshop with the aim of reaching, or even exceeding, the quota of forty tables needed for the launch of CountrySTAT in Benin."

a1722.speaker: Lokossou Orphée, representative of the General Directorate of Forests and Natural Resources (DGFRN)
a1722.name: Lokossou Orphée
a1722.title: representative of the General Directorate of Forests and Natural Resources (DGFRN)
a1722.speech: "These data are useful because they are part of what CountrySTAT needs. Indeed, to feed CountrySTAT, data are needed on the production of woody forest products produced in Benin: timber, service wood, fuel wood, the quantities imported or exported, the number of seedlings planted, the number of seedlings produced, etc. The data we supply also take into account information on wildlife: quantity killed per year, CITES specimens exported, annual quota, etc."

a1901.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1901.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1901.title: President of Ghana
a1901.speech: Has blamed Ghana's economic struggles on the 1966 overthrow of Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah, describing it as a setback that disrupted the country's path to industrialisation and self-sufficiency ; said the coup plunged Ghana into years of instability, delaying efforts to build a strong and self-reliant economy ; "Nkrumah envisioned an industrialised Ghana where citizens enjoyed high living standards rooted in patriotism and Pan-African unity. But on February 24, 1966, that dream was shattered, setting us back for decades."

a1901.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1901.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1901.title: President of Ghana
a1901.speech: Said removing Nkrumah opened the door to Ghana's growing reliance on foreign aid and economic policies that failed to prioritise local industries.

a1901.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a1901.name: John Dramani Mahama
a1901.title: President of Ghana
a1901.speech: Urged Ghanaians to reflect on the nation's journey, stressing that independence should not be viewed as a historical milestone alone but as a foundation for economic progress ; called for strong leadership and decisive action to break the cycle of missed opportunities and dependence on external assistance ; assured that his administration would push policies that promote local production, economic expansion, and self-sufficiency.

a1901.speaker: Declassified U.S. government documents
a1901.name: Declassified U.S. government documents
a1901.speech: Confirm that the coup was carried out with the involvement of the CIA as part of Western efforts to halt Nkrumah's economic policies and Pan-African agenda.

a2144.speaker: United Nations report / survey on children and armed conflict in Burkina Faso
a2144.name: United Nations report / survey on children and armed conflict in Burkina Faso
a2144.speech: Documented 2,483 serious violations of children's rights in Burkina Faso between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2024, against 2,255 children, with some experiencing multiple forms of abuse; it states that "1,386 children, some as young as eight months old, were killed and maimed, including by explosive devices," confirms the "abduction of 592 children, mainly girls," and the "recruitment and use of 257 children," predominantly boys, by armed actors; it notes that "twenty girls were raped, one of whom died as a result of gang rape," and attributes the majority of the grave violations to armed groups operating in the country.

a2144.speaker: United Nations
a2144.name: United Nations
a2144.speech: Underscores the dire humanitarian consequences of the intensified deadly armed attacks against civilians, which have led to the internal displacement of over two million people, the majority of whom are children; the organization estimates that 6.3 million people, including 3.4 million children, are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance, particularly in nutrition, health, protection and education.

a2144.speaker: Virginia Gamba, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict
a2144.name: Virginia Gamba
a2144.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict
a2144.speech: Expressed deep concern over the situation, warning that "the continuing deterioration of the security situation has particularly affected children's access to education, with more than 800,000 children affected by school closures."

a2144.speaker: Virginia Gamba, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict
a2144.name: Virginia Gamba
a2144.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for Children and Armed Conflict
a2144.speech: Called for the "full implementation" of the commitments made by the Burkinabe government, urging authorities to ensure accountability for perpetrators of violence against children and to provide access to justice and reparations for child victims; she also made a strong appeal to international donors to provide adequate funding for crucial reintegration programs.

a2144.speaker: United Nations report (progress findings)
a2144.name: United Nations report (progress findings)
a2144.speech: Highlights that the transitional government of Burkina Faso has approved a transfer protocol with the United Nations aimed at "ensuring that children presumed associated with armed forces and groups are transferred to civilian child protection services"; that "397 children formerly associated with armed forces and groups have benefited from reintegration services"; and that more than "700 officers from the defense and security forces have been trained" in human rights, with a specific emphasis on child protection principles.

a2243.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.name: Sam Matekane
a2243.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.speech: Appealed for greater financial assistance to least developed countries (LDCs) and landlocked developing countries (LLDCs) like Lesotho, speaking at the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FFD4) in Seville, Spain ; conveyed warm greetings from His Majesty King Letsie III, expressing gratitude to the Spanish government and its citizens for their hospitality ; drew attention to impediments such as climate change, substantial debt burdens, and restrictive trade policies, which he said obstruct advancements towards the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals ; characterised the FFD4 Summit as a "crucial moment for member states", saying that at a time when numerous countries, particularly across Africa, are grappling with severe economic constraints "we must renew our commitments to address the widening financing gap".

a2243.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.name: Sam Matekane
a2243.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.speech: Stressed the vital role of Official Development Assistance (ODA) for LDCs such as Lesotho, which face complex socio-economic issues such as high youth unemployment and insufficient public services in areas like education, health, and infrastructure: "The decline of ODA not only threatens our current advancements but also endangers our future prospects", urging development partners to fulfil their ODA commitments and consider establishing multi-year cooperation agreements for more predictable funding.

a2243.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.name: Sam Matekane
a2243.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.speech: Said trade was a fundamental driver of development, appealing to transit countries to implement more favourable policies to facilitate access to international markets for landlocked developing countries, and reiterated the call for developed nations to grant duty-free, quota-free access for all products originating from LDCs, in line with the provisions outlined in the FFD4 Outcome Document.

a2243.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.name: Sam Matekane
a2243.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.speech: "Developing nations must be empowered to mobilise domestic public resources for sustainable development" ; underlined the importance of collaborative efforts to combat illicit financial flows and improve tax systems, incorporating measures like digital taxation frameworks.

a2243.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.name: Sam Matekane
a2243.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.speech: Addressing the escalating debt crisis in sub-Saharan Africa, advocated for a reduction in borrowing costs and stressed the need for coordinated policies to foster long-term debt sustainability, stating, "We must work together to ensure vulnerable countries are not trapped in a cycle of unmanageable debt".

a2243.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.name: Sam Matekane
a2243.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.speech: Acknowledged the critical contribution of Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) to achieving the SDGs, asserting that "Investment in digital infrastructure is of paramount importance, especially for countries like Lesotho, to leverage digital transformation and enhance regional integration", highlighting the necessity of closing the digital divide, which disproportionately affects LLDCs.

a2243.speaker: Sam Matekane, Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.name: Sam Matekane
a2243.title: Prime Minister of Lesotho
a2243.speech: Echoed a collective call from member states for reforming the international financial architecture to make it more equitable and responsive to the needs of developing countries: "It is imperative that we create a financial system that serves us all, rather than one that perpetuates inequality".

a2243.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2243.name: Donald Trump
a2243.title: US President
a2243.speech: On April 2, dubbed "Liberation Day", announced a national emergency concerning his country's trade deficit and introduced "reciprocal tariffs" targeting all countries not under other sanctions.

a2250.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.name: Olavo Correia
a2250.title: Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.speech: Speaking to the press on the sidelines of the workshop on "Inter-island, International and Intermodal Connectivity and Digital Connectivity", stressed that the fact that Cabo Verde has been granted this third package demonstrates the recognition the United States of America has for the country, and also for the work that Cabo Verdean generations have done over recent decades.

a2250.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.name: Olavo Correia
a2250.title: Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.speech: Added that "the only priority" for the country is connectivity and land, air, maritime, digital and human mobility: "If we manage, with the support of the compact, to guarantee the best level of services, supply and governance with greater sustainability, and to place connectivity at the service of the diversification and the dynamic acceleration and economic management of Cabo Verde, we will be rendering, together with the United States of America, a great service to the Cabo Verdean nation, but above all to young Cabo Verdeans and to Cabo Verdean women on all the islands of Cabo Verde." ; said that in this sense the Government is committed to "making it happen" and, together with the strength and energy of the Cabo Verdean people, to working to deliver to the new generation a Cabo Verde that is "more engaged, more inclusive and with opportunities for all" citizens on the islands and in the diaspora.

a2250.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.name: Olavo Correia
a2250.title: Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.speech: Explained that the amount will be presented at a later stage, after the projects are presented, but stressed that the priority now is to know the results to be delivered to citizens, to address the reforms to be implemented, the projects to be developed and the objectives to be achieved: "After that, we will present it consistently, based on studies, based on analysis, with the involvement of the whole Cabo Verdean nation, and only then will we submit the justified envelope to the compact, and at that point we will then establish with the United States the amount that will be allocated to Cabo Verde."

a2250.speaker: Olavo Correia, Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.name: Olavo Correia
a2250.title: Minister of Finance and Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.speech: Said that at this moment it is necessary to have the strategic vision and everyone's understanding, to analyse the projects and fit them within the Government's vision for the future of the nation, which is to make connectivity and mobility "a pillar of acceleration and amplification" of opportunities in order to double the growth potential of the Cabo Verdean economy ; acknowledged that to overcome the challenges the country needs to act in fundamental areas, namely climate action, digital transition, connectivity and mobility, diversification of the national economy and the private sector, improving the business and investment environment, and human capital.

a2250.speaker: Joana Brito, coordinator of the Programme Development Unit (UDP)
a2250.name: Joana Brito
a2250.title: coordinator of the Programme Development Unit (UDP)
a2250.speech: Explained that studies have already been launched in these two areas and that they are at the stage of analysing the constraints.

a2250.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.name: Olavo Correia
a2250.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2250.speech: "The entire private sector will be directly involved in this process, as will all of civil society, and this consultation approach will be implemented throughout this process of developing the Compact."

a2263.speaker: Mohamed Youssouf Goumaneh, former member of parliament and friend of the ABED association
a2263.name: Mohamed Youssouf Goumaneh
a2263.title: former member of parliament and friend of the ABED association
a2263.speech: Thanked the ABED association and its friends in the Brussels diaspora for their generosity towards their fellow citizens of the Obock region.

a2263.speaker: Souleiman Omar, ABED representative in Djibouti
a2263.name: Souleiman Omar
a2263.title: ABED representative in Djibouti
a2263.speech: Recalled that the ABED association has, since its founding, supported projects to improve living conditions for populations in the interior regions and in the capital, as well as taking part in the country's social development.

a2263.speaker: Osman Ahmed (Talabo), project manager
a2263.name: Osman Ahmed (Talabo)
a2263.title: project manager
a2263.speech: Stressed that the association will continue its projects to help populations of the interior regions and, at the same time, plans to support other projects beneficial to his compatriots.

a2280.speaker: Donald Trump, United States President
a2280.name: Donald Trump
a2280.title: United States President
a2280.speech: In May, United States President Donald Trump accused South Africa of discriminating against whites in the country, citing Malema as the leader of an anti-white movement.

a2280.speaker: UK Home Office
a2280.name: UK Home Office
a2280.speech: In June, Malema was denied a visa to the United Kingdom because he was regarded as "non-conducive to the public good", according to the UK Home Office.

a2280.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2280.name: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2280.speech: The EFF described the move [the UK visa denial] as an act of "cowardice".

a2280.speaker: Western Cape Division of South Africa's Equality Court (ruling)
a2280.name: Western Cape Division of South Africa's Equality Court (ruling)
a2280.speech: Found Malema guilty of hate speech because of comments he made at a rally in Cape Town in October 2022, which the court said violated the country's Promotion of Equality and Prevention of Unfair Discrimination Act. ; The statements, the court found on Wednesday, could be interpreted as "a clear intention to incite harm". ; "Whilst calling out someone who behaves as a racist may be acceptable, calling for them to be killed is not," the court said in its ruling.

a2280.speaker: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2280.name: Julius Malema
a2280.title: leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2280.speech: Criticised his colleagues for not retaliating more forcefully. He urged them to "follow up" with one white man seen in the footage so that the man could be "attended to properly". Malema went on to say that "revolutionaries must not be scared to kill," and that racist acts should be interpreted as "an application to meet your maker with immediate effect". ; "No white man is going to beat me up... Revolution demands that at some point there must be killing," he said.

a2280.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement reacting to the ruling)
a2280.name: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) (statement reacting to the ruling)
a2280.speech: The EFF accused the court of presenting a "grave distortion" of history and political speech, and of "attacking" democracy. Malema's comments, the party argued, were made in relation to South Africa's history of apartheid and subsequent liberation movements, and were meant "theoretically". The EFF argued that the court had taken Malema's words out of context and disregarded the events surrounding it, including the Brackenfell school incident and the country's apartheid history. ; "This decision is fundamentally flawed and deliberately misreads both the context and the meaning of the speech," the EFF said. ; "When Malema spoke of 'war', it was a reference to the irreconcilable conflict between white supremacy and Black consciousness, a war of ideas and systems, not an instruction to kill people," the statement further read.

a2280.speaker: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2280.name: Julius Malema
a2280.title: leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF)
a2280.speech: In a comment [in 2009], Malema said the woman who had accused former President Zuma of rape "had a nice time" with Zuma.

a2280.speaker: Several South African experts
a2280.name: Several South African experts
a2280.speech: Have debunked this claim [of a 'white genocide'], however, and say there is no evidence that white people are being targeted for their race in the country.

a2280.speaker: Donald Trump, United States President
a2280.name: Donald Trump
a2280.title: United States President
a2280.speech: Has referred to Malema's speeches as evidence of an alleged "white genocide" in South Africa.
