Trump, as well as senior officials in his administration, including former adviser Elon Musk, have also backed claims by fringe white South African groups that a genocide of white people is taking place in South Africa. ; When President Cyril Ramaphosa visited the White House in May, Trump confronted his counterpart with old clips of Malema's rallies and songs and reiterated claims of whites being targeted. ; He also criticised South Africa for taking Israel to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on allegations that it is committing genocide in Gaza.

a2280.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a2280.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a2280.title: President of South Africa
a2280.speech: Explained that Malema's EFF is not part of the governing coalition government and is in opposition to the president's ANC party. He also told Trump that claims of white South Africans being targeted were false, although he acknowledged that the country is facing high crime rates.

a2280.speaker: Elon Musk, Trump's former adviser
a2280.name: Elon Musk
a2280.title: Trump's former adviser
a2280.speech: Has in the past posted clips of Malema's songs and accused the politician of "actively promoting white genocide".

a2280.speaker: Ronald Lamola, South Africa's Foreign Minister
a2280.name: Ronald Lamola
a2280.title: South Africa's Foreign Minister
a2280.speech: While speaking to the press, accused the US of preferential treatment of white South Africans and Washington of a second apartheid. The "refugee programme is preferential treatment of Afrikaners", Lamola said. "Preferential treatment of a particular privileged group, the Afrikaners, who are not running away from any genocide in this country, is definitely apartheid 2.0," he added.

a2289.speaker: Bah Oury, Prime Minister of Guinea
a2289.name: Bah Oury
a2289.title: Prime Minister of Guinea
a2289.speech: The Prime Minister expressed satisfaction with the IMF mission. Addressing the diagnosis of economic governance, the Head of Government stressed that certain aspects require improvement. "It is essential to combine our efforts to strengthen the capacity of public finances," he stated.

a2289.speaker: Bah Oury, Prime Minister of Guinea
a2289.name: Bah Oury
a2289.title: Prime Minister of Guinea
a2289.speech: Requested technical assistance from partners for the public services, in order to remedy weaknesses and strengthen the financial system. "Although the National Agency for the Fight against Corruption (ANLC) and the Court for the Repression of Economic and Financial Offences (CRIEF) are already operational, we are asking for additional technical support for these institutions, so that they can better detect tax fraud," he added.

a2289.speaker: Bah Oury, Prime Minister of Guinea
a2289.name: Bah Oury
a2289.title: Prime Minister of Guinea
a2289.speech: Reaffirmed the commitment of the President of the Republic and of the Government to put in place a mechanism similar to the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) of the United States. "This strategic vision makes it possible to change the game in terms of development," he concluded.

a2289.speaker: Press review on the page of the Prime Minister's Office of the Republic of Guinea
a2289.name: Press review on the page of the Prime Minister's Office of the Republic of Guinea
a2289.speech: According to a press review consulted by Guineenews.org on the page of the Prime Minister's Office, it is mentioned that, despite the limited time available to it, the IMF mission succeeded in establishing a relevant diagnosis of the country's economic situation.

a2289.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation
a2289.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation
a2289.speech: Took stock of the work carried out in collaboration with various sectors, covering in particular economic governance, public spending and projects requiring technical assistance from partners.

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: Says he is pleased he has been able to connect with the business world, and that he hopes to leverage off the participation of several dozen South Africans in the Obama administration's Young African Leader Initiative (YALI): "Through them, I hope I can grow my connections" into this young, vigorous community for the future.

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: "On the cultural side, in the States, I first learned about what was taking place in South Africa from writers I loved, from artists, from a poet like Sipho Sepamla, who wrote 'The Soweto I Love'... I got that book years ago from one of my labour union mentors, Jerry Hudson." ; "I know that one. That's just perfect." ; "It is artists like that who first told me the South African story.... I grew up in a highly political household, my father taught in the Congo and we kept up on the South African political situation." ; "I think he is amazing... and I really wish that someone like Sipho was better known to young South Africans; there doesn't seem to be enough emphasis on arts education and cultural education now."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: "My wife, Raina, is the most excited member of our household to be here; she's been drinking in the experience; especially whenever we go out beyond our residence, beyond the embassy, and have real exchanges with unsung heroes - mostly women - in the townships who are providing lifelines for people in the critical areas of health care and education." ; "On Mandela Day we volunteered in a primary school outside Tembisa to refurbish their library.... And the school we volunteered in, the headmaster was doing all he could, but with meagre resources; we were re-shelving books there that were forty years old. That doesn't seem fair."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: On the American art hung in the ambassador's residence: "I follow currents in art pretty closely and I knew artists who spoke to the moment and about the US and South Africa. The artists picked, asked some pretty serious questions about what we are doing to promote transformation in both cultures." ; Explains that Kehinde Wiley recycles the tradition of Renaissance portraiture, portraying black street kids in that style, and that this speaks to how South African artist Mary Sibande portrays her grandmother in a maid's uniform as a figure of dignity and nobility; says the art he and his wife picked is designed to encourage conversations that bring forth "disturbing courage and questioning - and hopefully leads to some kind of resolution."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: Says he still writes poetry to relax, although mostly it is "bad poetry," he laughs; on seeing Eve Ensler's "I Am an Emotional Creature" at the University of Johannesburg, "It was so exciting to see all the South African women who had come out to see it."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: "The one word I want associated with my time here in South Africa is 'investment'. We're already touched on President Obama's YALI program, that is an investment in the leaders here." ; "the region is attracting more foreign direct investment than foreign aid and that is a huge, huge deal.... We have to decide what that ought to mean for us." ; "last year, South Africa exported over 60,000 BMWs and Mercedes that were built out here (to America)." ; notes that the bilateral relationship has been transformed by that investment and the growing interdependence between the two nations.

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: On stability and the investment climate: "All of our economies have gone through a significant period of turbulence, post-2008, and we've all recovered at different rates and varying degrees... and it is a little disconcerting for some of us as we look at the environment here that certain pieces of legislation like the MPRDA, the private security bill and the agriculture bill... don't create an environment that is conducive to economic growth... they certainly give investors pause.... [While] investment is not a panacea, but for people on the periphery on the economy, all of us together need to puzzle this out... to close the skills gap so that young people can make their way up the skills ladder. We need more strategic initiatives like that, and more planning that speaks to the National Development Plan."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: Says that with AGOA up for renewal, President Obama supports that renewal; admits that reciprocity - South African restrictions on chicken and beef imports - could conceivably affect the climate towards AGOA; notes that PEPFAR continues to have a major impact in South Africa even though its total dollar commitment has been declining, and that PEPFAR's role is shifting as the South African government takes up a growing share of the cost: "AGOA, PEPFAR, these are both programs that share wide, bipartisan support in the Congress.... And Democratic and Republican members of the House feel just as strongly as the president does on this, although there are some issues to be worked out for resolution on market access." ; Insists AGOA is not a jobs transfer program sending jobs out of the US, and says economic success in Africa should generate more jobs and more demand for American goods and services: "Rooting for success here [in Africa], just means rooting for ourselves."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: Disagrees with the pre-emptive critique of the US-Africa Leaders Summit, arguing that given what he calls "an absolutely unprecedented in scale" meeting in the US, there will be robust conversation on increasing access to energy on the continent, greater food security, improvements in regional peace, and economic development: "I know that my South African counterparts with whom I have been engaging with for the past several months are excited by this." ; "We're going to walk away with a real road map about what our engagement ought to look like over the next few decades."

a2328.speaker: Critics (unnamed)
a2328.name: Critics (unnamed)
a2328.speech: Have charged that the US-Africa Leaders Summit is already set for failure by virtue of the lack of individual bilaterals between heads of state, or because of the absence of a full court press on specific investment plans.

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: On comparisons with China-Africa summits: agrees comparisons should be made, including on the trade relationship and the role of US companies in skills transfer and building up communities. "It's not an extractive relationship at all." Asked whether this was a veiled criticism of the Chinese: "No, I'm making a statement of fact about our real relationship"; "South Africans should ask the same tough questions of Chinese companies they ask of us."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: On the BRICS bank: says that if the new bank makes good investments in sustainable development, it can't really be a bad thing - "If it leads to the likelihood that we have more thoughtful, responsible planning around projects, it can't be a bad thing."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: On his UNISA speech about unions: "I don't know if I was tough, but it was an attempt to be candid in the hopes that, maybe, some of the hard lessons we learned in the States might make a contribution here when you are at a point when you are trying to make some determination about whether you have effective laws that already exist that govern the relationships between workers, industry and government - [this] at a time when everyone's got to be concerned about the legacy of Marikana and what that says." ; "It's been a tumultuous period, and we're no longer at the time where South Africa is just simply seen through the prism of the 'Madiba Magic'. Companies are making some really brutal decisions about where they are going to put their stake in the ground, based on what outcomes are going to look like for their bottom line. Workers need to have the most sophisticated recognition of that. There was an understanding - in America - seen through the concessions of the workers in the auto industry and the airline industry.... Even as we are so far away from the lofty standards - in both societies - we have set for ourselves.... But it cannot be a zero sum game... Folks need to figure out what other tools are in the tool kit before the 'nuclear option'."

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: On the NUMSA strike: points to the impact of the strike in the auto industry, noting that the strike in the Ford plant in Silverton has meant several thousand SUVs have not been made, and that this may have an adverse impact on decisions about future investment by the company; adds that this does not mean workers should not be agitating for better conditions, but everyone has to understand the interdependence of things.

a2328.speaker: Patrick Gaspard, US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.name: Patrick Gaspard
a2328.title: US Ambassador to South Africa
a2328.speech: Says in parting that South Africa is uniquely positioned to play a vital leadership role on the continent on regional peace and security and multilateral trade facilitation: "It is one we ought not to miss."

a2331.speaker: US State Department (statement)
a2331.name: US State Department (statement)
a2331.speech: "Throughout the trip, the Secretary will highlight how the United States has accelerated the partnership since the US-Africa Leaders Summit, including in areas such as climate, food and health security."

a2331.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2331.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a2331.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2331.speech: "Cabo Verde hopes to deepen the historic ties of friendship with the United States of America and to outline new forms of partnership in strategic areas for sustainable development"; noted the "great commitment" of the two countries to "universal values", both assuming the role of democratic states under the rule of law, respecting Human Rights.

a2331.speaker: China-Portuguese Speaking Countries Cooperation and Development Fund (CPD Fund)
a2331.name: China-Portuguese Speaking Countries Cooperation and Development Fund (CPD Fund)
a2331.speech: Said the delegation's visit to the archipelago, from Monday to Wednesday, has the aim of "strengthening cooperation between China and Cabo Verde in the area of investment and the identification of business opportunities in the country's strategic sectors".

a2331.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a2331.name: Government of Cabo Verde
a2331.speech: Reiterated on Wednesday its commitment to the "one China" principle, following the 12 January elections in Taiwan that brought William Lai to the presidency.

a2445.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi (Facebook post)
a2445.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2445.title: President of Malawi (Facebook post)
a2445.speech: Confirming the meeting via his Facebook page, said he was happy that the World Bank was committed to help Malawi improve its macro-economic landscape: “The World Bank says it is committed to help Malawi accelerate economic growth and transform livelihoods of its citizens.”

a2445.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a2445.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a2445.title: President of Malawi
a2445.speech: “During an interaction with Managing Director for World Bank responsible for operations, Anna Bjerde, at the bank's headquarters in Washington DC, we agreed on the importance of utilising the bank's fund for poorer countries, International Development Association (IDA),” ; said among the priority issues was the inclusion of Malawi as one of the 15 pioneering African economies to benefit from an ambitious project designed to provide electricity access to 300 million Africans by 2030, and that the World Bank understands that Malawi requires tailor-made interventions to bolster investments in clean energy as a catalyst to sustainable development.

a2445.speaker: World Bank
a2445.name: World Bank
a2445.speech: Says it is committed to help Malawi accelerate economic growth and transform livelihoods of its citizens.

a2723.speaker: Daniel Hagari, spokesman for the Israeli army
a2723.name: Daniel Hagari
a2723.title: spokesman for the Israeli army
a2723.speech: "Hamas did not comply with its obligations to first release the Israeli civilian women," in a brief statement made immediately after confirmation that the hostages had entered Israeli territory.

a2723.speaker: Israel (government)
a2723.name: Israel (government)
a2723.speech: expressed its disagreement on Friday night when Hamas announced it would release four female soldiers abducted from the Nahal Oz military base on 7 October 2023, arguing that one of the conditions of the agreement was that civilian women would have priority in the release.

a2723.speaker: Efe, Spanish news agency
a2723.name: Efe
a2723.title: Spanish news agency
a2723.speech: stating that it had had access to the documents, asserts that no clause mentions this priority.

a2723.speaker: Israeli press
a2723.name: Israeli press
a2723.speech: reported in recent days that Israel tried to press for Arbel Yehud to be one of the women released today.

a2723.speaker: Office of the Israeli Prime Minister (note)
a2723.name: Office of the Israeli Prime Minister (note)
a2723.speech: issued a note this morning stating that Tel Aviv will not allow Palestinians to return to the north of Gaza until hostage Arbel Yehud is released.

a2723.speaker: Islamic Jihad, Palestinian militant group
a2723.name: Islamic Jihad
a2723.title: Palestinian militant group
a2723.speech: claimed in November 2023 that one of the civilians, Shiri Silberman, who was abducted along with her husband, Yarden Bibas, and her children Ariel and Kfir, aged 5 and 2, had died in an Israeli attack, but the army has never confirmed the information.

a2723.speaker: Daniel Hagari, spokesman for the Israeli army
a2723.name: Daniel Hagari
a2723.title: spokesman for the Israeli army
a2723.speech: In a televised statement after the release of the hostages, acknowledged that the army is "deeply concerned" about the fate of the two children.

a2723.speaker: Israel (military/government)
a2723.name: Israel (military/government)
a2723.speech: confirmed that the hostages were well, shortly after the handover to the Red Cross.

a2723.speaker: Hamas (list of prisoners to be released)
a2723.name: Hamas (list of prisoners to be released)
a2723.speech: According to a list released by Hamas, Israel is due to release 200 Palestinian prisoners or detainees by the end of today, including 121 serving life sentences; the list indicated that 70 would be expelled from Gaza and the West Bank, but it was not indicated to where.

a2723.speaker: Hamas-run Interior Ministry (statement)
a2723.name: Hamas-run Interior Ministry (statement)
a2723.speech: said that displaced Palestinians will be able to return to the north of Gaza from Sunday; in a statement on Saturday, the ministry, which oversees the police forces, said that Palestinians will be able to move between the south and the north of Gaza on foot along the Rashid coastal road.

a2723.speaker: Israel (assessment)
a2723.name: Israel (assessment)
a2723.speech: believes that at least a third of the more than 90 prisoners still in Gaza were killed in the initial attack or died in captivity.

a2777.speaker: Kenedid Ibrahim Houssein, President of UPF-Djibouti (Union of the Francophone Press of Djibouti)
a2777.name: Kenedid Ibrahim Houssein
a2777.title: President of UPF-Djibouti (Union of the Francophone Press of Djibouti)
a2777.speech: In a speech delivered on the occasion, recalled the importance of the national media in raising awareness of children's rights and the role journalists can play in protecting and preserving children's rights ; stated that in Djibouti the question of childhood is a government priority and that it is an integral part of human rights.

a2777.speaker: Fayçal Oulmi, Communication Officer of UNICEF Djibouti
a2777.name: Fayçal Oulmi
a2777.title: Communication Officer of UNICEF Djibouti
a2777.speech: For his part stressed the importance of this prize for the promotion of children's rights in Djibouti ; explained to the participants the role played by UNICEF-Djibouti, which works with its partners to ensure that every child and every adolescent can survive and flourish in the best possible conditions.

a2855.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a2855.name: United Nations (UN)
a2855.speech: Issued an urgent appeal to the international community on Monday, warning that famine could spread further in Sudan if immediate funding is not secured.

a2855.speaker: Clémentine Nkweta-Salami, UN Humanitarian Coordinator in Sudan
a2855.name: Clémentine Nkweta-Salami
a2855.title: UN Humanitarian Coordinator in Sudan
a2855.speech: Said the recent cuts and suspensions of funds by the main donors could put an end to humanitarian aid that is crucial for millions of vulnerable people across the country ; “The sudden funding cuts by major government donors are dealing a catastrophic blow to humanitarian aid in Sudan, a country in the grip of one of the deadliest humanitarian crises of our time,” she warned in a statement, stressing that the main humanitarian organisations assisting nearly 21 million people in distress in Sudan risk no longer receiving the support they need ; “This is the moment when everything must be done to save lives. I call on all the main donors to reconsider their decision to cut funding for life-saving humanitarian aid in Sudan” ; also called on governments, charitable organisations, foundations and the private sector to step in to fill the void left by these cuts.

a3029.speaker: Kimberly Rosen, USAID/Ghana Mission Director
a3029.name: Kimberly Rosen
a3029.title: USAID/Ghana Mission Director
a3029.speech: “The United States is proud to partner with the Ghana Health Service to bring health services to remote communities.” ; “The boats will improve medical outreach providing immunisations, maternal and childcare, malaria, nutrition, and other health services to you — the people of Jomoro.”

a3029.speaker: Gabriel Yengliereh, Jomoro District Director of Health Services
a3029.name: Gabriel Yengliereh
a3029.title: Jomoro District Director of Health Services
a3029.speech: Emphasised the importance of the boats, noting, “None of the communities along the lagoon have a health facility, and reaching them by road is nearly impossible.” ; “With these new boats, we can now bring critical health services directly to these remote communities.”

a3038.speaker: Michael Abramowitz, Voice of America director
a3038.name: Michael Abramowitz
a3038.title: Voice of America director
a3038.speech: Said nearly his entire staff of 1,300 journalists, producers and assistants had been put on administrative leave, crippling a media broadcaster that operates in almost 50 languages ; “I am deeply saddened that for the first time in 83 years, the storied Voice of America is being silenced,” he said in a post on LinkedIn, saying it has played an important role “in the fight for freedom and democracy around the world.”

a3038.speaker: USAGM report to Congress (2024)
a3038.name: USAGM report to Congress (2024)
a3038.speech: According to its latest report to Congress, USAGM employs roughly 3,500 workers with an $886-million budget in 2024.

a3038.speaker: William Gallo, VOA Seoul Bureau Chief
a3038.name: William Gallo
a3038.title: VOA Seoul Bureau Chief
a3038.speech: Said on Sunday he had been locked out of all company systems and accounts: “All I've ever wanted to do is shoot straight and tell the truth, no matter what government I was covering. If that's a threat to anyone, so be it,” he said on Bluesky.

a3038.speaker: Kari Lake, former news anchor and Trump loyalist nominated to be director of VOA / USAGM senior adviser
a3038.name: Kari Lake
a3038.title: former news anchor and Trump loyalist nominated to be director of VOA / USAGM senior adviser
a3038.speech: Issued a statement describing USAGM as “a giant rot and burden to the American taxpayer” and said it was “not salvageable” ; said she would shrink the agency to its minimum possible size under the law.

a3038.speaker: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (website notice)
a3038.name: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (website notice)
a3038.speech: Notes on its website that it has been declared an “undesirable organization” by the Russian government and warns readers in Russia and Russia-occupied Ukraine that they could “face fines or imprisonment” for liking or sharing its content.

a3038.speaker: Jan Lipavsky, Czech Foreign Minister
a3038.name: Jan Lipavsky
a3038.title: Czech Foreign Minister
a3038.speech: Said Radio Free Europe had been a “beacon” for populations under totalitarian rule: “From Belarus to Iran, from Russia to Afghanistan, RFE and Voice of America are among the few free sources for people living without freedom,” he wrote on X.

a3038.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order)
a3038.name: Donald Trump
a3038.title: US President (executive order)
a3038.speech: Signed an executive order on Friday instructing USAGM and six other little-known agencies to reduce their operations to the minimum mandated by statutes, saying it was necessary to shrink bureaucracy.

a3038.speaker: Mike Balsamo, president of the National Press Club in Washington
a3038.name: Mike Balsamo
a3038.title: president of the National Press Club in Washington
a3038.speech: Released a statement saying the cuts at VOA undermined America's commitment to a free and independent press: “For decades, Voice of America has delivered fact-based, independent journalism to audiences worldwide, often in places where press freedom does not exist.”

a3038.speaker: Reporters Without Borders (Paris-based)
a3038.name: Reporters Without Borders (Paris-based)
a3038.speech: Blasted the move, saying it “threatens press freedom worldwide and negates 80 years of American history in supporting a free flow of information.”

a3038.speaker: Bay Fang, president of Radio Free Asia
a3038.name: Bay Fang
a3038.title: president of Radio Free Asia
a3038.speech: Said the cancellation of its funding was “a reward to dictators and despots, including the Chinese Communist Party, who would like nothing better than to have their influence go unchecked.”

a3038.speaker: Some Republicans
a3038.name: Some Republicans
a3038.speech: Have accused VOA and other publicly funded media outlets of being biased against conservatives, and have called for them to be shuttered as part of the efforts by tech billionaire Elon Musk and his Department of Government Efficiency to shrink the government.

a3038.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a3038.name: Elon Musk
a3038.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency
a3038.speech: Made light of the cuts to USAGM: “While winding down this global government propaganda agency, it has temporarily been renamed the Department of Propaganda Everywhere (DOPE),” he wrote on X.

a3038.speaker: White House (statement)
a3038.name: White House (statement)
a3038.speech: Said in a statement that his executive orders “will ensure that taxpayers are no longer on the hook for radical propaganda,” before listing various criticisms of VOA, including allegations of left-wing bias.

a3167.speaker: Gautier Mignot, European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.name: Gautier Mignot
a3167.title: European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.speech: has warned against too much dependence on humanitarian aid, especially in meeting the objectives set out in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

a3167.speaker: Gautier Mignot, European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.name: Gautier Mignot
a3167.title: European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.speech: According to Mignot, the EU leverages on private sector investments and resources through its Global Gateway Strategy, to ensure that the rest of the world, and in particular Nigeria's critical sectors - energy, agriculture, education, health, and digital - are supported to bring sustainable development to the people ; noted that the EU is the first provider of official development aid globally: "More or less, 42 percent of the Official Development Assistance (ODA) comes from the EU and its Member States."

a3167.speaker: Gautier Mignot, European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.name: Gautier Mignot
a3167.title: European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.speech: called for cooperation between the EU, Nigeria, and Africa; noted that only through cooperation and shared interests and values - respect for individual rights and human rights, respect for the rule of law, civil liberties, and democracy - will the continent, particularly Nigeria, achieve sustainable development in all its sectors.

a3167.speaker: Gautier Mignot, European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.name: Gautier Mignot
a3167.title: European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.speech: urged citizens of the country, particularly young people, to eschew unverified information by fact-checking to determine their authenticity: "It is very important to avoid and detect disinformation; fact-check to debunk fake news. It is a service to you and your community. You should all feel responsible, not only for not spreading fake news, but to help debunk them." ; "We promote a society model that is respectful of culture and religious differences, is tolerant, based on civil liberties, and social inclusion. This is why some of our rivals try to undermine us, propagating lies and disinformation about what we are and what we stand for, particularly in West Africa." ; "Our Union is based first in values, respect for individual rights and human rights, respect for the rule of law, civil liberties, and democracy. It is based on institutions which are democratically elected. It is based on the rights of citizens, especially the rights of free movement of people, goods and services, and capital. It is based on laws and legislation adopted by all institutions." ; "We want to extend to the rest of the world the same recipe that has made us successful. It is the recipe of cooperation, equal rules for all, respect for all nations' rights and legitimate interests, respect for the rights of individuals, and shared prosperity with strong innovation capacities."

a3167.speaker: Gautier Mignot, European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.name: Gautier Mignot
a3167.title: European Union Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS
a3167.speech: Assuring Nigeria of the EU's continued and reliable partnership for sustainable development, he said: "What we want is not a relationship based on donor-beneficiary relation; we want a relationship based on partnership and mutual interests and based on investments in particular" ; explained that the aim is because, if you look at the Official Development Assistance (ODA) by itself, it will not be sufficient to reach the SDGs which we all adopted in 2015 as shared common goals of the whole international community.

a3167.speaker: Ahmed Mohammed Abdullahi, Registrar, Skyline University
a3167.name: Ahmed Mohammed Abdullahi
a3167.title: Registrar, Skyline University
a3167.speech: described the visit of the EU Delegation to the university as timely and momentous, emphasised the importance of dialogue, collaboration, and mutual understanding in a constantly evolving global landscape: "The lecture series titled 'The European Union, a reliable partner of Nigeria and the world,' is timely and momentous. This occasion is a testament to the enduring and fruitful partnership between the European Union and our academic community, reinforcing the importance of dialogue, collaboration, and mutual understanding in a constantly evolving global landscape." ; "Conversations here encourage meaningful discussions that not only highlight contemporary challenges, but also extend innovative solutions for world peace, prosperity, and development."

a3263.speaker: OCHA Mozambique (Situation Report No. 1, in collaboration with humanitarian partners)
a3263.name: OCHA Mozambique (Situation Report No. 1
a3263.title: in collaboration with humanitarian partners)
a3263.speech: Reports that in June a total of 83,983 people were displaced by attacks in Ancuabe and Chiure districts, the majority (approx. 67,524) women and children; that violence had a spill-over effect in Nampula province where 23,000 displaced people arrived; that to date partners have supported 29,000 people with multisectoral assistance out of 50,000 targeted; that in Pemba authorities have requested the support of the humanitarian community to relocate approx. 2,000 IDPs to new resettlement sites in Ancuabe due to concern over overcrowding; and that on 19 July humanitarian partners met with local authorities and agreed to organize 'go and see visits' by IDPs to the identified relocation areas in Ancuabe.

a3263.speaker: IOM/DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix data)
a3263.name: IOM/DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix data)
a3263.speech: According to IOM/DTM, a total of 83,983 people were displaced throughout June, the majority of them being women and children (67,524); as many as 69,031 of the movements recorded represent individuals displaced for the first time, and some 23,774 people were also displaced to Nampula province as a result of the attacks.

a3263.speaker: Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) Cluster
a3263.name: Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) Cluster
a3263.speech: Reports that an estimated 33 per cent of the newly arrived population requires shelter assistance, 23 per cent requires food assistance, 13 per cent requires access to water, and the remaining 31 per cent requires access to other needs like latrines and hygiene kits.

a3263.speaker: Joint Government and inter-agency assessment mission (5 July)
a3263.name: Joint Government and inter-agency assessment mission (5 July)
a3263.speech: The mission concluded that N'naua was not a viable alternative; differently, the site of Nanona could accommodate a limited expansion up to a maximum of 1,000 people.

a3263.speaker: Assessment team
a3263.name: Assessment team
a3263.speech: Noted that as more people are expected to move into the site, less land would be available for cultivation, making people dependent on food assistance.

a3263.speaker: Humanitarian community / humanitarian partners
a3263.name: Humanitarian community / humanitarian partners
a3263.speech: Has been advocating with authorities that movements to these sites should happen only after intention surveys are concluded and analysed and basic services are put in place, and that security in these locations is also key ; Advocated for targeted humanitarian assistance to newly displaced people in Pemba city, to reduce their suffering in the face of the overcrowding conditions in the city.

a3263.speaker: Intention surveys of 82 IDPs conducted by Emergency Protection Units in Pemba (11 July)
a3263.name: Intention surveys of 82 IDPs conducted by Emergency Protection Units in Pemba (11 July)
a3263.speech: Results demonstrated a need to: 1) ensure better information sharing with the impacted population to ensure informed decision (few had information on upcoming plans); 2) advocate for more options for IDPs (since some wanted to remain in Pemba and others be re-located to sites other than Ancuabe); and 3) advocate for greater protection support to vulnerable IDPs in Pemba.

a3263.speaker: Local authorities in Pemba / Cabo Delgado
a3263.name: Local authorities in Pemba / Cabo Delgado
a3263.speech: Requested the support of the humanitarian community to relocate 2,000 newly displaced people from Pemba to two areas identified for new resettlement sites in Ancuabe district, in an effort to decongest Pemba city ; Agreed to organize 'go and see visits' by IDPs to Nanona site and other areas going forward, and agreed to consider existing resettlement sites as alternative options to relocate other IDPs that are currently not intending to return to Ancuabe.

a3367.speaker: Traders Advocacy Group Ghana (TAGG) (statement)
a3367.name: Traders Advocacy Group Ghana (TAGG) (statement)
a3367.speech: Made an urgent and impassioned plea to the Government of Ghana, calling for the immediate procurement of a modern, state-of-the-art aircraft for the exclusive use of the President of the Republic, stating they are deeply concerned by the "inconveniences and risks" recently faced by President John Mahama during his official travels: "Ghana, a nation blessed with abundant resources such as gold, oil, and other minerals, must rise above pettiness and face this national challenge with seriousness and urgency." ; argued that if frequent-flying traders understand the "frustrations and trauma" of unreliable travel, it is unacceptable for the nation's First Gentleman to be subjected to the same ; "We cannot afford another tragedy or national calamity before action is taken," emphasizing that "Protecting the President is equivalent to protecting the sovereignty and future of Ghana." ; cautioned the government against seeking a short-term fix, demanding "value for money by acquiring a durable, modern aircraft—not outdated or substandard equipment that puts lives at risk."

a3367.speaker: Traders Advocacy Group Ghana (TAGG) (statement)
a3367.name: Traders Advocacy Group Ghana (TAGG) (statement)
a3367.speech: Concluded its release by laying out three non-negotiable pillars of its position: the safety of the President is non-negotiable; the dignity of Ghana must be upheld internationally; the aircraft must be a national asset, not a partisan tool.

a3439.speaker: Osabarima Ansah Sasraku, Chief of Mamfe Akuapem (chairman of the event)
a3439.name: Osabarima Ansah Sasraku
a3439.title: Chief of Mamfe Akuapem (chairman of the event)
a3439.speech: In his address emphasised that family planning is a fundamental human right, enabling individuals to make informed choices about their socio-economic futures.

a3439.speaker: Dr. Patrick Kuma Aboagye, Director-General of the Ghana Health Service
a3439.name: Dr. Patrick Kuma Aboagye
a3439.title: Director-General of the Ghana Health Service
a3439.speech: Acknowledged the progress made but also called for collective efforts to combat myths and misconceptions that hinder access to Family Planning services.

a3439.speaker: USAID and UNFPA Ghana (solidarity messages)
a3439.name: USAID and UNFPA Ghana (solidarity messages)
a3439.speech: Urged increased domestic financing for family planning.

a3439.speaker: Alex Kwasi Acquah, Deputy Minister of Health
a3439.name: Alex Kwasi Acquah
a3439.title: Deputy Minister of Health
a3439.speech: Officially launched the Costed Implementation Plan, expected to cost $114 million, and reaffirmed the government's commitment to its smooth implementation.

a3529.speaker: Abubakar Malami, former Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice (petition)
a3529.name: Abubakar Malami
a3529.title: former Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice (petition)
a3529.speech: The petition, dated 10th September 2025 and addressed to the National Security Adviser, Director General of the Department of State Services, Inspector General of Police, and the Comptroller-Generals of Immigration and Civil Defence, purportedly raises alarm about alleged plans to destabilize Kebbi State through the importation of political thugs, mercenaries from Niger Republic, and the trafficking of arms, and further accuses the sitting governor of Kebbi of complicity, even going as far as linking the state government to terrorist networks ; alleges that foreign mercenaries from Niger Republic are being armed and deployed to Kebbi; claims thugs roam freely, attacking citizens without fear of law enforcement; insists that Governor Nasir Idris and his allies are complicit, and even mentions links to a terrorist network.

a3529.speaker: Nasir Idris, Governor of Kebbi State
a3529.name: Nasir Idris
a3529.title: Governor of Kebbi State
a3529.speech: Has consistently reaffirmed his government’s zero tolerance for banditry, terrorism, and thuggery.

a3745.speaker: Sónia Abreu, Marketing Director of Société Générale Mozambique
a3745.name: Sónia Abreu
a3745.title: Marketing Director of Société Générale Mozambique
a3745.speech: Said the delivery of one hundred mattresses and mosquito nets, repellents, clothes donated by employees and non-perishable food products is a joint mobilization between the company and the employees in a humanitarian assistance gesture ; “For the Bank, each person represents the future and Société Générale will always be willing to support the collective needs of the communities where we operate”.

a3745.speaker: Sara Matimele, Director of Human Resources, Société Générale Mozambique
a3745.name: Sara Matimele
a3745.title: Director of Human Resources, Société Générale Mozambique
a3745.speech: “this act is not only an act of corporate responsibility, but also a gesture of love and compassion that touched each employee, because of the sad images we saw in the media. It could have been one of us in this situation, so the message we also want to pass on to society in general is that we are for the future, for the reconstruction of the economy, which is why we are here.”

a3745.speaker: Júlia Ferrão, representative of the Repensar Cooperative
a3745.name: Júlia Ferrão
a3745.title: representative of the Repensar Cooperative
a3745.speech: Praises this initiative and ensures that this aid will significantly change the lives of communities in a time after the cyclone ; “Right now we have families getting back together and they need mattresses for example, notwithstanding the need to prevent diseases like malaria and cholera that are prone to this time”.

a3828.speaker: Machesetsa Mofomobe, Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3828.name: Machesetsa Mofomobe
a3828.title: Basotho National Party (BNP) leader
a3828.speech: Described the 90-day pause of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) at a press briefing at the BNP Centre in Maseru on Tuesday as the ‘Worst thing to have happened to Lesotho’ ; lamented the fact that ‘the government is quiet about the situation while jobs are certain to be lost’ ; said countries such as Botswana, eSwatini and South Africa have addressed their nations about the USAID pause and have allocated funds on how they plan to conquer the looming crisis in the next 90 days ; pleaded with Prime Minister Ntsokoane Matekane to lead the nation through the crisis ; unveiled his recommendations to the government, which include helping employees of US-funded programmes with interest waivers on their loans with local banks and a three-month stipend for 90 days.

a3828.speaker: Donald Trump’s incoming administration (announcement)
a3828.name: Donald Trump’s incoming administration (announcement)
a3828.speech: Announced that there will be an audit on USAID all across the world and that all funds as well as donations will be put on hold for a period of 90 days, which is approximately three months.

a3828.speaker: Janice Nkajja, Ugandan woman (social media post, quoted on Malawi Voice)
a3828.name: Janice Nkajja
a3828.title: Ugandan woman (social media post, quoted on Malawi Voice)
a3828.speech: Said it is wrong for Africa to have depended on US donations till today with no plan for alternative survival: “We have depended on USAID for over 60 years, and the moment the owners of the money say, ‘Let’s take a 90-day pause so that I audit where my money is going,’ suddenly the whole country goes into a frenzy” ; said this should rather be a moment of reflection for the African continent in general, adding “We have been asking for a very long time to be liberated from colonialism, neo-colonialism, and now that the opportunity presents itself, for some reason we are complaining” ; “This is just a 90-day pause. What would happen if the United States just said, ‘We’re not giving you money anymore?” ; said Africans should actually start looking for systems that are sustainable which would make life easier without foreign aid.

a3975.speaker: The New York Times
a3975.name: The New York Times
a3975.speech: Reported today that a stockpile of contraceptives worth 10 million dollars, destined for developing countries, was destroyed by the United States Agency for International Development.

a4057.speaker: Rogério Uthui, STV commentator/analyst
a4057.name: Rogério Uthui
a4057.title: STV commentator/analyst
a4057.speech: argues that the latest attacks on the Niassa reserve may be intended to distract the authorities; for him there is no doubt that terrorism's main interest is Cabo Delgado province, because of the megaprojects. "I understand this attack on the reserve as being exactly for diversion, so much so that the reserve is almost 40 thousand km² of land that has no population. We cannot be attacking zones [without population], it makes no sense."

a4057.speaker: Rogério Uthui, STV commentator/analyst
a4057.name: Rogério Uthui
a4057.title: STV commentator/analyst
a4057.speech: argues that the announcement of TotalEnergies' return to Cabo Delgado, together with the announcement made by the North American President, Donald Trump, of the opening of banks to finance the 5 billion gas exploration project, may have attracted those who want to halt the country's gas project. "It is natural that these attacks intensify at exactly this moment when all the logistics are being assembled again for the restart of works on the gas plant in Palma. So, without any doubt, I see that there is a cause-and-effect relationship here."

a4057.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a4057.name: Donald Trump
a4057.title: President of the United States
a4057.speech: announced the opening of banks to finance the 5 billion gas exploration project.

a4199.speaker: Shariff Ali Sharif, Minister of State in the President’s Office for Labour, Economy and Investment (Tanzania)
a4199.name: Shariff Ali Sharif
a4199.title: Minister of State in the President’s Office for Labour, Economy and Investment (Tanzania)
a4199.speech: Said the week-long festival, running from September 20 to 27, has been organised by the Zanzibar Economic Empowerment Agency (Zeea) in collaboration with the Tanzania Trade Development Authority (TanTrade): “This forum, which will be held on the opening day of the festival, will discuss how products from Zanzibar can benefit by gaining markets in those countries” ; said two important sectors, tourism and trade, are expected to benefit directly, as stakeholders will discuss the best ways to improve markets for goods and services from Zanzibar ; “These exhibitions will provide an opportunity for products from Zanzibar to be seen and promoted through this special platform, targeting both the national and international markets.”

a4199.speaker: Yasmin Chali, Managing Director of Airpay, the main sponsor of the festival
a4199.name: Yasmin Chali
a4199.title: Managing Director of Airpay, the main sponsor of the festival
a4199.speech: Said they will strengthen digital empowerment in the delivery of services: “We recognise and value the efforts to empower entrepreneurs and grow their businesses; our collaboration is to ensure that financial systems meet the needs.”

a4199.speaker: Juma Burhan, Director of the Zanzibar Economic Empowerment Agency (Zeea)
a4199.name: Juma Burhan
a4199.title: Director of the Zanzibar Economic Empowerment Agency (Zeea)
a4199.speech: Said they have already reached more than 180 people who have come forward, so they will sell and get the opportunity to promote themselves internationally.

a4249.speaker: Human Rights Watch (rights group)
a4249.name: Human Rights Watch (rights group)
a4249.speech: Said at least 120 children have been abducted by insurgents in Mozambique and that there had been a resurgence of attacks and child kidnappings in the last two months; called on Mozambique's government to do more to find the children and prevent further abductions.

a4249.speaker: Witnesses
a4249.name: Witnesses
a4249.speech: Have said that children abducted from towns and villages have been used as fighters in subsequent attacks.

a4249.speaker: United Nations
a4249.name: United Nations
a4249.speech: According to the United Nations, the violence has displaced more than 600,000 people and spilled into neighboring provinces.

a4249.speaker: Jan Egeland, Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council
a4249.name: Jan Egeland
a4249.title: Secretary General of the Norwegian Refugee Council
a4249.speech: Visited Cabo Delgado this month and described the situation in northern Mozambique as a neglected crisis ; “Climate shocks, increasing violence and spiralling hunger are having a terrible impact on the population.”

a4249.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a4249.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a4249.speech: Said more than 5 million people faced critical levels of hunger and more than 900,000 people faced emergency hunger conditions.

a4249.speaker: Marijke van der Lee (@anamafalda1992), social media post
a4249.name: Marijke van der Lee (@anamafalda1992)
a4249.title: social media post
a4249.speech: “Mozambique: Armed Group's Child Abductions Surge in North https://t.co/yN4Yx7YaOW #newspapers #feedly” — June 24, 2025.

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: "First of all it is my passion for livestock farming, and then I saw that you can make money in livestock farming. It is a job just like working in an office. I told myself that you earn more money than in an office." ; "I gave up everything to do this. I don't want to tell you that I am rich, but I am free. I am free in this field. I work with people and it is a flexible schedule."

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: Recalled of his Senegalese employer in France, Babacar Daou: "He let me travel to see birds all over France."

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: "That is one of the hazards of livestock farming." ; "I import pigeons to resell them, but I also export them to other countries. I sell pigeons as far away as Bangladesh. Everything I have in life, I owe to pigeon breeding." ; said the Saanen goat from Switzerland costs 800,000 CFA francs a head and can give three to four litres of milk a day ; of the South African breed: "It is a breed that gives meat." ; "It is a small farm here. I have partners. Often we can bring in 200 head that we resell. I send animals just about everywhere..."

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: "Since I have been here, I have had no support from the State." ; "The State must really improve its policy with regard to livestock. I emphasise livestock because it is my field. The State must change its policy, based on my experience as a young livestock farmer and entrepreneur. I have been to several countries and I have seen how it works there." ; believes that the structures that have been set up and that have little impact must get closer to livestock farmers and work with them, citing former Senegalese President Macky Sall's policy of importing Brazilian dairy cattle: "That will develop the country and prevent the importing of powdered milk."

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: Called on young people to become entrepreneurs and avoid settling into an office: "Being an entrepreneur does not necessarily mean being a livestock farmer; it can be in another field." ; "The family must also help us a great deal. For example, let the child choose to do what he really wants to do. Many young people want to start businesses but the family wants them to work in the administration, in offices and so on." ; suggested the government better support young graduates of schools such as the IPR of Katibougou: "I was recently invited there and I saw young people working in agro-pastoral activities and others in livestock farming. We can support them..."

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: Acknowledged that young entrepreneurs face serious difficulties in Mali, notably the lack of funds: "that must not be a reason to sit with our fingers crossed..." ; lamented that animal feed is very expensive in Mali ; "Thanks to me, many people have come to love livestock farming."

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: "I have written two guides on livestock farming (one on pigeon breeding and the other on goat breeding)."

a4330.speaker: Yehia Ismaila Dicko, young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.name: Yehia Ismaila Dicko
a4330.title: young Malian livestock farmer and owner of the Animalerie farm
a4330.speech: Said of Abou Kane, President of Senegal's livestock farmers: "It is sheep farming that makes him a billionaire."

a4330.speaker: Diallo, intern at the Animalerie farm and student at the Alou Kone polytechnic school
a4330.name: Diallo
a4330.title: intern at the Animalerie farm and student at the Alou Kone polytechnic school
a4330.speech: "We learn a lot of things with him and he is available for us. He shows us everything that is essential in livestock farming... After our studies, he will help us build our own business."

a4500.speaker: Police (Kenya)
a4500.name: Police (Kenya)
a4500.speech: Police say some of the sugar being consumed locally is smuggled from the main Kenya-Somalia border.

a4500.speaker: Police (Kenya)
a4500.name: Police (Kenya)
a4500.speech: The driver and his loader were taken into custody pending arraignment, police said.

a4500.speaker: Officials
a4500.name: Officials
a4500.speech: Officials say some of those involved in the business bribe their way to be able to pass through many security checks, while others use unauthorized routes to evade detection by security agencies.

a4535.speaker: BRICS summit documents (first summit, Yekaterinburg 2009)
a4535.name: BRICS summit documents (first summit
a4535.title: Yekaterinburg 2009)
a4535.speech: Contained explanatory reasons for creating the BRICS bank as ‘operating financial activities mainly based on non-interference, equality, and mutual benefit’ among members and other developing countries.

a4535.speaker: Central Bank of Russia
a4535.name: Central Bank of Russia
a4535.speech: Highlighted the main benefits of a BRICS payment system alternative to SWIFT as backup and redundancy in case there were disruptions to the SWIFT system.

a4535.speaker: BRICS report (July 2024)
a4535.name: BRICS report (July 2024)
a4535.speech: Reports that China launched its alternative to SWIFT, the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System; that India has its Structured Financial Messaging System (SFMS); and that Russia has SPFS and Brazil Pix.

a4535.speaker: World Bank report (2023)
a4535.name: World Bank report (2023)
a4535.speech: States that Ethiopia seeks to chart a development path that is sustainable and inclusive in order to accelerate poverty reduction and boost shared prosperity, and that achieving these objectives will require addressing key challenges: macroeconomic private sector development, structural transformation and job generation; reducing the incidence of conflict and overcoming the effects of the coronavirus pandemic; addressing food insecurity growing due to adverse weather events, locust invasion, conflict and global conditions leading to high inflation of food prices; improving human capital, which is far lower than the Sub-Saharan Africa average; and generating good jobs for a workforce growing by roughly 2 million persons reaching working age per year.

a4535.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual report (2024)
a4535.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) annual report (2024)
a4535.speech: Has rated Egypt as one of the top countries in Africa undertaking economic reforms.

a4535.speaker: World Bank
a4535.name: World Bank
a4535.speech: Reports that remittances, money earned by Egyptians living abroad and sent home, reached a record $21 billion in 2023.

a4535.speaker: Dilma Rousseff, President of the BRICS New Development Bank
a4535.name: Dilma Rousseff
a4535.title: President of the BRICS New Development Bank
a4535.speech: “The bank should play a major role in the development of a multipolar, polycentric world. Russia is a very important partner in BRICS and the New Development Bank, and is really fulfilling all of its commitments. And, indeed, the bank is facing a number of problems, primarily concerning liquidity.” (See Kremlin report - July 26, 2023)

a4535.speaker: Vladimir Putin, President of Russia (quoted on the Kremlin website)
a4535.name: Vladimir Putin
a4535.title: President of Russia (quoted on the Kremlin website)
a4535.speech: “Our development strategy for the 2022–2026 period aims to draw about 30 percent of our funds from domestic markets. It is also very important to attract funds in different currencies, not just dollars or euros. We are well aware of the difficulties encountered by the developing nations in their bid to attract investment. They need resources to finance infrastructure projects, develop digital and social logistics, and, of course, to reach their goals in environmental protection. Everyone is focused on their debt, ignoring their need for resources. It seems unacceptable to impose certain terms and requirements on them in exchange for funding like multilateral international organisations are doing now.”

a4535.speaker: BRICS New Development Bank (bank documents and operators)
a4535.name: BRICS New Development Bank (bank documents and operators)
a4535.speech: The bank’s documents show interest in engaging in traditional sectors such as alternative energy, information, telecommunications and new medical technologies, processing of mineral resources and working towards agricultural production growth; the bank operators declared confidence that cooperation, as frequently put “reliable and mutually beneficial partnership relations”, would benefit the developing countries and their peoples, and that cooperation among BRICS members has a great future.

a4535.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank (Pittsburgh G-20 summit, 2009)
a4535.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank (Pittsburgh G-20 summit
a4535.speech: Both financial institutions pledged forms of support for economic growth in developing countries. (See IMF and World report, June 2009)

a4535.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) official report (Article IV consultation with South Africa, June 2023)
a4535.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) official report (Article IV consultation with South Africa
a4535.title: June 2023)
a4535.speech: An official summarized report indicated that the IMF concluded the Article IV consultation with South Africa, whose economy is facing mounting economic and social challenges.

a4535.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) update (August 2024)
a4535.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF) update (August 2024)
a4535.speech: Reports that, as part of Ethiopia’s macroeconomic reform program endorsement, foreign creditors have granted financing assurances to Ethiopia enabling the government to fast-track approval of new loans by the IMF and the World Bank, with an official creditor committee offering firm assurances to restructure loans and outstanding debts.

a4535.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4535.name: Abiy Ahmed
a4535.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4535.speech: Told parliament in July 2024 that expected talks with the Washington-based IMF and World Bank could unlock more than $10 billion in financing in the coming years.

a4813.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a4813.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a4813.speech: says spending for the September 16 General Election poses “significant fiscal risks” and other policy missteps that threaten economic growth ; says the situation could be compounded by increased geopolitical tensions, global trade wars and reduced external financing ; maintains that expenditure has continued to outpace revenue growth, leading to widening fiscal deficits, while domestic revenue has increased from 12.5 percent of GDP in 2022 to 18 percent in 2024.

a4813.speaker: AfDB Malawi 2025 Country Focus Report, ‘Making Malawi’s capital work better for its development’
a4813.name: AfDB Malawi 2025 Country Focus Report
a4813.title: ‘Making Malawi’s capital work better for its development’
a4813.speech: “Major risks to the growth and macroeconomic stability outlook include a tepid recovery, high inflation, food insecurity, vulnerabilities in the banking sector and a protracted delay in resolving the debt crisis and climate shocks. The government needs to moderate its expansionary fiscal policy to support tight monetary policy efforts from the central bank.” ; “Emerging risks, including aid cuts and heightened protectionism, require the government to reduce dependence on aid, diversify the economy and export markets, including fully adapting to the continental trade market. Moreover, putting in place a structured diaspora labour market and mobilising remittances through formal channels must be accompanied by appropriate exchange rate policies.”

a4813.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a4813.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a4813.speech: has since proposed two policy options to accelerate economic development, notably boosting agricultural productivity through mega farms and mechanisation as well as actualising the agriculture, tourism, mining and manufacturing (ATM+M) strategy; says the success of mega farms will hinge on ensuring that all completed water infrastructure investments are fully utilised to maximise returns; says a critical enabler would be the creation of a conducive business environment to attract both domestic and foreign private capital; and said the ATM strategy’s success would be dependent on ensuring that necessary skills are available either by developing them locally or by revising the temporary residence policy to attract skilled foreign labour where needed.

a4813.speaker: World Bank’s Malawi Economic Monitor
a4813.name: World Bank’s Malawi Economic Monitor
a4813.speech: also said recently that election year spending and the need to absorb some critical expenditures, including those previously financed through the now dwindling aid inflows, will widen the budget deficit.

a4813.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a4813.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a4813.title: President of Malawi
a4813.speech: insisted that Malawi opted out of the Extended Credit Facility because the Bretton Woods institution was pushing for a fresh kwacha devaluation, upward adjustment of fuel prices and electricity tariffs and freezing some social spending.

a4813.speaker: World Bank
a4813.name: World Bank
a4813.speech: recently called for increasing domestic revenues through reforms to increase the progressivity of the tax system and the efficiency of tax administration, reducing wasteful spending; also urged phasing out the implicit fuel subsidy, implementing reforms to enable the mining sector to support growth over many decades, removing foreign exchange surrender requirements and reducing trade barriers.

a4835.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB), Namibia
a4835.name: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a4835.title: Namibia
a4835.speech: said the sector is now facing a limited supply of market-ready animals across various marketing channels.

a4835.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB), Namibia
a4835.name: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a4835.title: Namibia
a4835.speech: said last year's drought had placed severe pressure on farmers, forcing many to increase cattle sales in response to harsh environmental conditions; said the increased marketing in 2024 had led to significant herd reductions, leaving farmers with limited market-ready animals this year.

a4835.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB), Namibia
a4835.name: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a4835.title: Namibia
a4835.speech: noted: "While slaughtering at domestic abattoirs has been affected by the overall industry contraction, the impact has been less severe than that on live exports"; also reported a 22% decline in slaughtering at export-approved abattoirs during the quarter under review.

a4835.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB), Namibia
a4835.name: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a4835.title: Namibia
a4835.speech: reported, on the lumpy skin disease movement restrictions south of the veterinary cordon fence: "These restrictions placed upward pressure on prices due to the reduced supply of animals at auctions."

a4835.speaker: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB), Namibia
a4835.name: Livestock and Livestock Products Board (LLPB)
a4835.title: Namibia
a4835.speech: reported that in the first quarter of 2025 a total of 281 906 kg of hides and skins, in the form of bovine wet blue and processed, were exported to South Africa, Zimbabwe, the UK and China, and that hides and skin imports totalled 165 976 kg during the quarter under review.

a4872.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique (communiqué)
a4872.name: Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique (communiqué)
a4872.speech: According to a communiqué from the Presidency of the Republic, the Head of State will preside, at Zinave National Park in Mabote district, over the ceremony marking the 50th anniversary of the Banhine and Zinave National Parks.

a4914.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4914.name: Marco Rubio
a4914.title: US Secretary of State
a4914.speech: Said on Monday the United States was cancelling 83% of programmes at USAID. “After a 6-week review, we are officially cancelling 83% of the programmes at USAID,” Rubio said on social media platform X. “The 5 200 contracts that are now cancelled spent tens of billions of dollars in ways that did not serve, (and in some cases even harmed), the core national interests of the United States.” ; Rubio said the remaining 1 000 programmes would be administered by the State Department.

a4914.speaker: Critics (unnamed)
a4914.name: Critics (unnamed)
a4914.speech: Warn that slashing USAID's work will affect millions of people across around 120 countries.

a4914.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a4914.name: Marco Rubio
a4914.title: US Secretary of State
a4914.speech: On Monday notably thanked the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which billionaire Elon Musk is leading in a drive to cut federal spending and jobs ; Rubio has reportedly criticised Musk over his aggressive belt-tightening.

a4914.speaker: Elon Musk, head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a4914.name: Elon Musk
a4914.title: head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
a4914.speech: Responded on X describing the USAID cuts as “tough, but necessary.”

a4914.speaker: US State Department
a4914.name: US State Department
a4914.speech: Had announced last month its intention to cut 92% of USAID contracts, identifying 5 800 grants to be eliminated.

a4914.speaker: Donald Trump and his allies
a4914.name: Donald Trump and his allies
a4914.speech: Have argued that foreign assistance is wasteful and does not serve US interests ; Trump has called for the humanitarian agency to be shut down and signed an executive order in January demanding a freeze on all US foreign aid to allow time to assess overseas expenses.

a4914.speaker: Aid groups
a4914.name: Aid groups
a4914.speech: Argue much of the assistance supports US interests by promoting stability and health overseas.

a4922.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a4922.name: World Food Programme (WFP) (statement)
a4922.speech: “In April 2025, funding shortfalls will force the WFP to suspend food and nutrition assistance to two million crisis-affected people, including Sudanese refugees in Chad, Malian refugees in Mauritania, internally displaced people and vulnerable families affected by food insecurity in Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Nigeria” ; stated that it urgently needs 620 million dollars, around 570 million euros, to guarantee the continuation of support to people affected by the crisis in the Sahel and Nigeria over the next six months ; recalled that the latest regional food security assessment shows West Africa is in the midst of a severe food and nutrition security crisis, stressing that an estimated almost 53 million men, women and children will face acute hunger between June and August of this year.

a4922.speaker: Margot van der Velden, WFP Regional Director for West Africa
a4922.name: Margot van der Velden
a4922.title: WFP Regional Director for West Africa
a4922.speech: “We anticipate that millions of people face emergency levels of hunger at the peak of the lean season, so the world must step up support to prevent this situation from spiralling out of control” ; “Inaction will have serious consequences for the region and beyond, since food security is synonymous with national security.”

a4922.speaker: Regional food security assessment (December 2024)
a4922.name: Regional food security assessment (December 2024)
a4922.speech: Shows that West Africa is in the midst of a severe food and nutrition security crisis, with an estimated almost 53 million men, women and children facing acute hunger between June and August of this year.

a4946.speaker: Members of the Chollo (Shilluk) community representing four counties in Upper Nile State, including political leaders
a4946.name: Members of the Chollo (Shilluk) community representing four counties in Upper Nile State
a4946.title: including political leaders
a4946.speech: Have raised deep concern over ongoing armed violence in their areas which they say has displaced 5,000 people and created a dire situation; blamed the violence on the SPLA-IO forces and armed allied militia against the position of Necessary Unified Forces in the region.

a4946.speaker: Hon. Rebecca Joshua Okwachi, member of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly representing Panyikang County (speaking on behalf of the Chollo communities)
a4946.name: Hon. Rebecca Joshua Okwachi
a4946.title: member of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly representing Panyikang County (speaking on behalf of the Chollo communities)
a4946.speech: "We, the Shilluk (Chollo) communities of the four counties—Panyikang, Makal, Fashoda, and Manyo strongly condemn and denounce the military attacks by the SPLA-IO forces on Nyiluak, Pakwa and Obai, in Panyikang County, Upper Nile State," ; "The attacks resulted in the displacement of an estimated 5,000 civilians, with the displacement extending into villages in Makal County, thereby destabilizing the lives of residents in both Fashoda and Manyo counties."

a4946.speaker: Hon. Rebecca Joshua Okwachi, member of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly representing Panyikang County
a4946.name: Hon. Rebecca Joshua Okwachi
a4946.title: member of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly representing Panyikang County
a4946.speech: Stated that on March 26 armed confrontations occurred in the town of Tonga, leading to the displacement of between 3,000 and 4,000 people from Tonga and surrounding areas; said the displaced persons have since sought refuge in Liri, a border area in South Kordofan, Sudan; added that further violence was reported on March 31 in the Thor-Gwang area of Manyo County, displacing an estimated 2,000 families.

a4946.speaker: Hon. Rebecca Joshua Okwachi, member of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly representing Panyikang County
a4946.name: Hon. Rebecca Joshua Okwachi
a4946.title: member of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly representing Panyikang County
a4946.speech: Urged all armed actors to prioritize peace and the protection of civilians; said the Chollo community "expresses condolences" to bereaved families and called on the national government to urgently intervene to de-escalate tensions and support peace efforts; urged the Upper Nile State authorities to provide emergency humanitarian aid to the displaced populations and ensure their protection: "We call on the national government to intervene urgently to address this critical situation. Thirdly, we urge the Upper Nile State government to take care of the citizens who have fled as a result of these events and to provide them with immediate humanitarian assistance." ; appealed to all armed groups operating in the area, including those reportedly from neighboring Jonglei State, to immediately end looting, destruction of property, and hostilities.

a4946.speaker: Chollo communities (collective statement)
a4946.name: Chollo communities (collective statement)
a4946.speech: Further called for the peaceful withdrawal of any forces currently occupying Tonga, the administrative capital of Panyikang County, and emphasized the need for a return to lawful and stable governance in the area.

a4946.speaker: SPLA-IO / the accused side (non-response)
a4946.name: SPLA-IO / the accused side (non-response)
a4946.speech: "Eye Radio was unable to immediately reach the accused side for comment."

a4959.speaker: United States government
a4959.name: United States government
a4959.speech: Has announced that the foreign aid promised to Mozambique under the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) will be disbursed, despite fears that the Trump administration would destroy the MCC, just as it has dismantled the US Agency for International Development (USAID).

a4959.speaker: US Embassy in Maputo (Thursday release)
a4959.name: US Embassy in Maputo (Thursday release)
a4959.speech: "following the foreign aid review, the MCC Board of Directors met in August and recommended that the Compact for the Connectivity and Coastal Resilience of Mozambique should go ahead" ; the recommendation "reflects that continued trust in the cooperation between the United States and Mozambique, stressing the commitment to generate tangible results for the two peoples" ; the Compact "is fully aligned with the priorities of US foreign policy, and seeks to produce concrete benefits for Mozambicans and Americans. These improvements stress the commitment of the US government to responsibility, transparency and measurable results, ensuring that the investment of American taxpayers promotes mutual prosperity".

a4959.speaker: Abigail Dresser, US charge d'affaires in Mozambique
a4959.name: Abigail Dresser
a4959.title: US charge d'affaires in Mozambique
a4959.speech: "the decision to press ahead with the Compact shows the commitment of both countries to build a stronger and more prosperous future. In refining the focus of the programme, we are guaranteeing that American investment creates opportunities for Mozambicans, at the same time as it promotes the stability and economic growth that benefits both our nations."

a4959.speaker: 2023 MCC document on the Compact
a4959.name: 2023 MCC document on the Compact
a4959.speech: Noted that "two-thirds of the Mozambican population resides along the coast, which is impacted by frequent and increasingly intense cyclones, flooding, and natural disasters that overwhelm local transport networks, large and small-scale agriculture, community opportunity, and societal cohesion"; the Compact "aims to address these multifaceted risks through projects that will strengthen local economies that are reliant upon agriculture and fisheries yet limited by connectivity and reliable access".

a4959.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4959.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a4959.speech: Describes itself as "an independent US government agency working to reduce global poverty through economic growth".

a5055.speaker: Report “Unpacking Africa's Debt: Towards a Lasting and Durable Solution” by the UN Special Adviser on Africa (UN OSAA), launched 14 November 2024
a5055.name: Report “Unpacking Africa's Debt: Towards a Lasting and Durable Solution” by the UN Special Adviser on Africa (UN OSAA)
a5055.title: launched 14 November 2024
a5055.speech: States that borrowing remains a necessary tool to navigate the compounding crises of financial distress, climate change, food insecurity, and persistent conflict; emphasizes the need to re-examine Africa's historical reliance on debt instruments to address structural constraints and unlock economic opportunities; emphasizes the need to reform the global financing system to ensure predictable and affordable financing, prioritize development outcomes over private finance interests, and create fiscal space to fund SDG investments ; says existing frameworks, including debt restructuring arrangements like the Common Framework, are insufficient to meet Africa's development needs.

a5055.speaker: Cristina Duarte, Under-Secretary-General and Special Adviser on Africa to the UN Secretary-General
a5055.name: Cristina Duarte
a5055.title: Under-Secretary-General and Special Adviser on Africa to the UN Secretary-General
a5055.speech: “Debt is an important mode of financing. While many countries are in debt distress, we must not treat Africa as a completely debt-distressed continent,” said at the launch of the report in New York ; “Debt, when managed effectively, can help us invest in achieving development goals.”
