a5109.speaker: Choguel Kokalla Maiga, outgoing Prime Minister of Mali
a5109.name: Choguel Kokalla Maiga
a5109.title: outgoing Prime Minister of Mali
a5109.speech: Openly criticized the military in power, notably accusing them of taking unilateral decisions without prior consultation with him ; Expressed his dissatisfaction publicly regarding crucial decision-making concerning the extension of the political transition, from which he felt sidelined ; Launched a virulent attack against Major General Abdoulaye Maiga, the main target of the ex-PM's charges at the clarification rally of 15 November 2024.

a5109.speaker: Communiques from associations and organizations supporting the Army
a5109.name: Communiques from associations and organizations supporting the Army
a5109.speech: The day after the ex-PM's outburst, communiques poured in to support the Army and the new Prime Minister, General Abdoulaye Maiga.

a5109.speaker: Nelson Mandela (quoted)
a5109.name: Nelson Mandela (quoted)
a5109.speech: “After climbing a great hill, one only finds that there are many more hills to climb. I have taken a moment here to rest, to steal a view of the glorious vista that surrounds me, to look back on the distance I have come. But I can rest only for a moment, for with freedom come responsibilities, and I dare not linger, for my long walk is not yet ended.”

a5274.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a5274.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a5274.title: President of Malawi
a5274.speech: Has emphasised the need for construction of more modern feeder roads to facilitate easy mobility of goods within districts. Chakwera said being a country that largely depends on agriculture, it is a must for government to improve the transport infrastructure including in rural communities where most of the farming activities take place. "We want to connect more areas to the M1 and the lakeshore roads so that there is easy transportation of agricultural produce. The American Government is assisting us with the road from Kasungu to Mkanda in Mchinji, but we have to add other roads on our own," Chakwera said.

a5274.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a5274.name: Lazarus Chakwera
a5274.title: President of Malawi
a5274.speech: Said his government is revitalising the agriculture sector to promote food security and spur agro-based economic activities.

a5274.speaker: Traditional Authority Chisinga
a5274.name: Traditional Authority Chisinga
a5274.speech: While thanking government for giving out agriculture loans through the Economic Empowerment Fund, asked for the speedy disbursement of the loans ; He also thanked government for constructing 12 houses for police and other security agencies, saying they will boost security in the area which is close to the Zambian border.

a5274.speaker: Bauden Mtonga, Member of Parliament for Kasungu North West Constituency
a5274.name: Bauden Mtonga
a5274.title: Member of Parliament for Kasungu North West Constituency
a5274.speech: Said dry spells and straying elephants have contributed to food shortages in the area, asking government to increase numbers for those to benefit from relief maize. "I am happy to report that the construction of the perimeter fence around Kasungu National Park is nearing completion. This is good news for us and our farming activities, giving hope that this year we will harvest more crops," Mtonga said.

a5499.speaker: Supporters and members of the Liberation for Economic Freedom Party (LEFP)
a5499.name: Supporters and members of the Liberation for Economic Freedom Party (LEFP)
a5499.speech: Have expressed strong confidence in Mbewe's leadership and believe his candidacy represents hope for a new era in Malawi's politics.

a5507.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a5507.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a5507.title: President of Tanzania
a5507.speech: Speaking at the launch, emphasised the CBT's crucial role in supporting underserved communities, particularly the nation's small-scale farmers, by providing them with the affordable financial tools needed to overcome challenges and thrive in their agricultural endeavours.

a5507.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a5507.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a5507.title: President of Tanzania
a5507.speech: Counselled that the CBT should operate with the same diligence, transparency and adherence to regulations as any other reputable financial institution, fully complying with the Bank of Tanzania's (BoT) guidelines.

a5507.speaker: Historical studies on the cooperative movement in Tanganyika
a5507.name: Historical studies on the cooperative movement in Tanganyika
a5507.speech: Reveal the remarkable reach of the cooperative movement in Tanganyika during that period, with cooperatives managing 49 per cent of the country's annual exports; only Israel and Denmark had cooperative systems that handled a greater proportion of their nations' overseas trade.

a5507.speaker: Further research on Tanzanian peasant cooperatives
a5507.name: Further research on Tanzanian peasant cooperatives
a5507.speech: Highlights the success of Tanzanian peasant cooperatives in effectively organising markets for their members and providing essential inputs at affordable costs, leading to a significant boom in both cash and food crop production; between 1954 and 1968, Tanganyika stood out as the only African state that consistently achieved a food production growth rate exceeding its population growth.

a5546.speaker: Financial Times poll (published earlier this week)
a5546.name: Financial Times poll (published earlier this week)
a5546.speech: Revealed that 60% of Americans agreed with the freeze on American international aid under USAID, taken by Donald Trump and implemented by Elon Musk; only 12% of those polled disagreed with the idea that significant amounts of aid funds are wasted on corruption and administrative costs, to the detriment of those who really need them.

a5611.speaker: Ambassador Abukar Osman Baalle, Somalia’s Permanent Representative to the UN
a5611.name: Ambassador Abukar Osman Baalle
a5611.title: Somalia’s Permanent Representative to the UN
a5611.speech: strongly condemned Israel’s actions against civilians in occupied Palestinian territories and called for immediate international intervention; underscored Somalia’s unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people, denouncing the escalating violence in Gaza and expressing deep concern over the humanitarian crisis: “Somalia is gravely concerned about the deteriorating situation in Gaza and the ongoing atrocities faced by the Palestinian people. We strongly urge Israel to respond to the international community’s calls for restraint and to allow unhindered humanitarian assistance to those in need” ; “The civilian population, especially women and children, faces critical challenges, including acute food shortages and worsening malnutrition. The international community must act swiftly to prevent further escalation.”

a5702.speaker: Thomas Andrew Fahn, prominent citizen of Gbarpolu County and former Representative candidate for District #3
a5702.name: Thomas Andrew Fahn
a5702.title: prominent citizen of Gbarpolu County and former Representative candidate for District #3
a5702.speech: described the closure as “long overdue” and called for a full investigation into the role of local and national officials in enabling the company’s controversial operations ; “They extracted massive amounts of iron ore while ignoring community development, labor rights, and environmental safety” ; “This should not be swept under the rug” ; describes the Chinese-owned Bio-Chico a “disaster for Liberia,” commending the Boakai Administration for revoking the company’s operational permits; speaking on Prime FM in Monrovia, said Bio-Chico’s presence brought exploitation, contract violations, and unethical labor practices to the region ; “If you do a survey in the county, you’ll find that only a clique of those in authority benefitted from Bio-Chico, while ordinary citizens were enslaved and robbed of their mineral resources”; accused members of both the Gbarpolu County local authority and the Liberian Legislature of colluding with the company ; “This matter goes beyond shutting down one company. We must hold accountable those in government, who enabled this exploitation to happen under their watch.”

a5702.speaker: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah, Information Minister of Liberia
a5702.name: Jerolinmek Mathew Piah
a5702.title: Information Minister of Liberia
a5702.speech: made the pronouncement during a press briefing at MICAT in Monrovia; said the decision followed a high-level inter-ministerial meeting convened by President Joseph Nyuma Boakai on May 14 at the Executive Mansion ; “President Boakai instructed that all permits associated with the road transport of ore by Bio-Chico be immediately revoked” ; “No Bio-Chico truck transporting iron ore will not be allowed to use public roads anymore”; said the meeting brought together key ministries, Justice, Mines and Energy, Public Works, Transport, and State, in response to growing public concerns; revealed the company had been operating under a permit issued by a single government agency, without undergoing the required multi-ministerial review; emphasized the company was required to transport ore to a stockpile site near a jetty and wait until construction of the jetty was completed before initiating exports, and noted the failure to comply directly prompted the government’s decision to revoke its permits.

a5901.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a5901.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a5901.speech: Revised downwards its forecasts for global economic growth for 2025 and 2026, lowering them from 3.3% (January 2025 estimate) to 2.8% and 3% respectively.

a5901.speaker: World Trade Organization (WTO) study
a5901.name: World Trade Organization (WTO) study
a5901.speech: Reveals that, given disparities in levels of economic development and economic power, American tariff policies will only exacerbate global inequalities between rich and poor countries; the least developed countries will suffer the most severe consequences, which will seriously compromise the achievement of the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

a5901.speaker: United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)
a5901.name: United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO)
a5901.speech: Warns that these unjustified protectionist measures undermine the potential of developing countries and least developed countries to participate fully in world trade, thereby wiping out their efforts at industrial modernisation and economic diversification, amounting to depriving nations, in particular those of the global South, of their right to development.

a5901.speaker: China (sponsored communiqué from the partner)
a5901.name: China (sponsored communiqué from the partner)
a5901.speech: States that the abusive imposition of customs duties by the United States is a typical practice of unilateralism, protectionism and economic hegemonism, reflecting a “zero-sum game” mentality and serving as a new tool of disguised protectionism aimed at diverting internal tensions through a trade war ; says that as the largest developing country and a responsible member of the international community, China has taken legitimate and firm countermeasures, defending both its sovereign interests and the rules of international trade and global economic justice ; says China is aware that yielding to hegemony would amount to “drinking poison to quench one’s thirst”, that history has proved concessions only embolden bullies, and that “China will not kneel, and it will never back down.”

a5901.speaker: China (sponsored communiqué from the partner)
a5901.name: China (sponsored communiqué from the partner)
a5901.speech: Calls on China and African countries, including Burkina Faso, to close ranks around mutual respect, equality, win-win cooperation and shared prosperity, to defend the rules-based multilateral trading system centred on the WTO, and says China is ready to share development opportunities with Burkina Faso, notably through zero-tariff treatment on 100% of its imports from Burkina Faso, and encourages competent and reliable Chinese companies to invest and build factories in Burkina Faso and transfer technology ; urges the firm choice of multilateralism and an equal and orderly global multipolarity, of fairness and justice – development being a universal right, not a privilege – and of win-win cooperation ; says it is convinced this retrograde and unpopular tariff war is doomed to failure, and that China will seize the opportunity of implementing the results of the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation to work with African countries for the solidarity and empowerment of the “global South”.

a5926.speaker: Crayton O. Duncan, Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia, Chair of the Senate Committee on Concessions
a5926.name: Crayton O. Duncan
a5926.title: Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia, Chair of the Senate Committee on Concessions
a5926.speech: Expressed serious disappointment and disdain over enactment of law protecting foreign companies from being grilled, X-rayed, and interrogated on the floor of plenary; speaking on a live midnight talk show, the Heat, said it’s very saddening that the Liberian Senate will enact a law to prevent foreign companies from being invited by Plenary, when the United States Congress invites and questions foreign companies regarding their operations ; “This is what hurts me, when you want to invite or bring these concession companies or big companies on the senate floor to grill them, the 54th Liberia Senate passed a rule, which we met there that prevents companies from being invited for interrogation and grilling. And so, who do you think told them not to do that, are the very white or Western people? Look at TikTok, Huawei, and other companies in the United States that were invited to Congress for questioning and grilling. But, in Liberia, the West had bought us not to bring companies on the floor. And I heard that sometimes, it was because of Firestone, based on the radical approach from the Liberian Senate towards the company. They did so, and Firestone was angry, therefore, today, no concession companies are allowed to come to the plenary for questioning. Our resources that these guys are exploiting, so we don’t have the right to call and grill them. The fear of the white man is one of the main reasons our country is like this”.

a5926.speaker: Crayton O. Duncan, Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.name: Crayton O. Duncan
a5926.title: Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.speech: Said that if the leadership of the country, especially the Executive and the Legislature, can only take responsibility by consciously knowing that they are responsible for the failure of Liberia and rethink and adjust the direction of the country, Liberia will be great ; “But, do you know why we can’t do that? We are not man enough to look in the faces of the white and say the truth. We are a nation and one people. We need to look in their faces and tell them that international best practices are not helping us. We can do it, yes, but that is where the breviary comes in. This has to be done by President Joseph N. Boakai, because people believe that he would make the hard decision based on his age, but we are not seeing it. We have to reexamine all concession agreements and change the laws that harm our people and prevent foreign companies”.

a5926.speaker: Crayton O. Duncan, Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.name: Crayton O. Duncan
a5926.title: Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.speech: Accused Western Power of resisting Liberia’s development and economic growth, while urging the Executive Branch of government to prioritize and focus on self-initiatives aimed at addressing pressing infrastructure and developmental challenges; believes that Liberia’s development is about self-initiative, rather than aid dependency, stressing the need to desist from relying on foreign aid to develop the country; urged the Senate plenary, policymakers, and stakeholders to desist from relying on the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank for Liberia’s development and instead embark on self-initiatives, noting that the World Bank and the IMF can’t develop Liberia because it will go against their interest, and that these institutions were created to develop Europe and America based on their motives, but through the sweat and blood of African resources.

a5926.speaker: Crayton O. Duncan, Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.name: Crayton O. Duncan
a5926.title: Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.speech: “There are two ideologies in the world today. One is from the West, they believe in playing and influencing our minds through seminars, workshops, and symposiums, known as capacity development. If you notice the west, they will have many symposiums in Liberia. Their primary reason is to control the way we think and behave. They will never turn that into development. If you think about the US$200 million the Liberian people are paying for the nation’s stable food we eat every year, you will be afraid. The West will never allow Liberia to engage in agricultural self-sufficiency in food production. I bet the government to do that, they will never allow it” ; indicated that the West has established itself in Indo-China, where it is being used to supply the World Market with food, therefore anyone who wants to resist Liberia spending such money on food will end up like the late President William R. Tolbert ; “When President Tolbert said in 1980 that there will be no imported rice to Liberia, the only thing we were looking at was the Congo attitude. But nobody knows why Tolbert died here. I’m saying all of these things to encourage us to open our eyes. Challenge Firestone, let them produce something here. Stop being afraid to face the reality.”

a5926.speaker: Crayton O. Duncan, Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.name: Crayton O. Duncan
a5926.title: Senator of Sinoe County, Liberia
a5926.speech: Stated that the US$800 Million declared by Bea Mountain Mining Company in Grand Cape Mount County last year as the benefits of what they exported from Liberian gold and diamond is clearly another statement to demonstrate the exploitation in the sector ; “This tells you that they exported over a billion dollars’ worth of gold. In the Central Bank, our national budget is US$700 million, while Bea Mountain is exporting our gold worth a billion. We have to take the initiative to strengthen our economy and build our roads. It’s a challenge for us. We need to stop the Executive from behaving the way they are, without any accountability for our resources. It’s important for us to take our resources back into our hands to reexamine this so-called concession call international best practices”.

a5926.speaker: Bea Mountain Mining Company (declaration to the Liberian Senate)
a5926.name: Bea Mountain Mining Company (declaration to the Liberian Senate)
a5926.speech: Declared US$800 million in Grand Cape Mount County last year, telling the Liberian senate and the country at large that such amount was the benefits of what they exported from Liberian gold and diamond.

a6028.speaker: World Bank
a6028.name: World Bank
a6028.speech: Announced a revision of the international poverty line, raising the minimum threshold from US$2.15 a day (Sh5,614) to US$3.00 (Sh7,834) a day ; according to the World Bank, these changes are intended to keep pace with changes in world price levels and to give a more realistic picture of the minimum standard of living, especially in low-income countries ; stressed that the method of measuring extreme poverty has not changed, what has changed is better data and surveys from poor countries.

a6028.speaker: Dr Thobias Swai, Senior Lecturer at the Business School, University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM)
a6028.name: Dr Thobias Swai
a6028.title: Senior Lecturer at the Business School, University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM)
a6028.speech: Said the raising of the threshold has no direct effect on citizens, except that it will affect the formulation and implementation of national policies for fighting poverty. "This is only an average, and it does not mean that the cost of living will rise starting today; it means that it has been rising ever since they issued the last assessment. What will be affected there is policy formulation, because the number of the extremely poor will now increase" ; said it is now the duty of policymakers to update existing policies: "Policies will be affected more, and even their implementation will have to change, because if there were 15 million poor people, now they may increase to 20 million, so you need more investment in projects to lift people out of poverty since their number is now increasing."

a6028.speaker: Aziz Rashid, Lecturer in Financial Economics, Ardhi University
a6028.name: Aziz Rashid
a6028.title: Lecturer in Financial Economics, Ardhi University
a6028.speech: Said the new thresholds are an indicator and a reflection of the reality of many people's lives, saying the Sh7,800 cited is enough to eat in the country but cannot cover other essential needs. "The increase in that threshold is a sign of the increase in human needs, because even that threshold of $3 (Sh7,834) may be enough only for food, but there are further needs such as shelter, clothing and even medical treatment, so the needs are greater than even that threshold" ; advised that great effort be invested in increasing food production and skills among citizens so they obtain more income enabling them to live above those thresholds.

a6028.speaker: Dr Mwinuka Lutengano, economics lecturer, University of Dodoma (UDOM)
a6028.name: Dr Mwinuka Lutengano
a6028.title: economics lecturer, University of Dodoma (UDOM)
a6028.speech: Said the important thing is to consider the national threshold, because the international threshold is often higher than the domestic one. "Given the state of the world economy, even national poverty lines will undoubtedly rise if we align them with the new ones that have been set" ; "Therefore, we must continue to strengthen ourselves economically through sustained efforts. This includes strategic investment and increasing national revenue. Ultimately, our goal is robust economic growth and ensuring that this growth benefits all citizens."

a6066.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6066.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a6066.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6066.speech: reiterated Somalia’s strong support for the Palestinian cause; PM Hamza firmly rejected Israel’s recent statements regarding the displacement of Palestinians, emphasizing that such actions constitute clear violations of international law, human rights, and existing agreements. “The Federal Government of Somalia stands in full solidarity with the Palestinian people in their just struggle for an independent state,” he stated, praising their resilience in the face of adversity.

a6066.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6066.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a6066.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6066.speech: addressed the crises in Sudan and Syria, reaffirming Somalia’s commitment to the stability and territorial integrity of both nations while advocating for non-interference in their internal affairs.

a6066.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6066.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a6066.title: Prime Minister of the Federal Republic of Somalia
a6066.speech: expressed gratitude to Arab nations for their continuous support to Somalia in the areas of security and humanitarian assistance. He called on Arab investors to explore opportunities in Somalia’s agriculture, livestock, and energy sectors to foster long-term development and economic growth.

a6093.speaker: Mohamed Abdi Hayir, Somali Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation
a6093.name: Mohamed Abdi Hayir
a6093.title: Somali Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation
a6093.speech: said the funds, part of broader international support, are intended to alleviate the significant hardships faced by impoverished farmers in Puntland. He emphasized that this aid was allocated solely to address the dire needs of the people, with no consideration for the ongoing political disputes between the federal and regional governments ; underscored that the decision to allocate these funds was made with the best interests of the Puntland population in mind, particularly the farmers grappling with food insecurity. "The federal government sent $16 million to Puntland despite the current political climate, driven by its commitment to the people it governs, especially the impoverished farmers of the region."

a6093.speaker: Mohamed Abdi Hayir, Somali Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation
a6093.name: Mohamed Abdi Hayir
a6093.title: Somali Minister of Agriculture and Irrigation
a6093.speech: In response to Puntland's accusations that it had not received its fair share of tractors distributed by the federal government to regional states, Abdi dismissed these claims as a "smokescreen." He raised concerns that the funds intended to support farmers and pastoralists in Puntland may have been misappropriated. "When I encountered these baseless accusations, I began to question whether the funds allocated to support Puntland's farmers and pastoralists had been misused. The allegations against us appear to be a diversion." ; further called on Puntland authorities to cease making "groundless accusations" and instead focus on fulfilling their responsibility to procure the remaining tractors necessary for the region's agricultural development. "They must cease these false claims and take decisive action to acquire the remaining tractors for the benefit of Puntland's farmers."

a6093.speaker: Puntland authorities
a6093.name: Puntland authorities
a6093.speech: have vehemently rejected the comments and countered that the federal government has failed to honor its commitments.

a6093.speaker: Somali federal government
a6093.name: Somali federal government
a6093.speech: claiming it dispatched food aid supplies to Puntland, a statement that regional officials have adamantly denied.

a6099.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6099.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6099.speech: said on Wednesday that governments in sub-Saharan Africa have provided school meals to roughly 20 million extra children over the past two years, showing a move away from dependence on foreign aid and a stronger commitment to education.

a6099.speaker: WFP report
a6099.name: WFP report
a6099.speech: "Government investments in school meals ... (signal) a significant shift from reliance on foreign aid to recognising school meals as a strategic public investment in children's education (and) health," the report said. ; The WFP report found that local farmers had also benefited from the school feeding. The government of Benin's buying local food for these programmes contributed over $23 million to the economy in 2024, it said. More than a third of school meals in Sierra Leone came from food produced by smallholder farmers. ; It warned, however, that millions of children, especially in some of the lowest income African countries like the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Somalia, and South Sudan, still lacked access to school meals, as donor support continued to fall.

a6099.speaker: U.N. report (end of July)
a6099.name: U.N. report (end of July)
a6099.speech: A U.N. report at the end of July found that more than one in five Africans, 307 million, were chronically malnourished, meaning hunger is worse than two decades ago. It predicted the continent would have 60 per cent of the world's hungry people by 2030.

a6141.speaker: Senator Godswill Obong Akpabio, Senate President of Nigeria
a6141.name: Senator Godswill Obong Akpabio
a6141.title: Senate President of Nigeria
a6141.speech: “I am convening an emergency closed session with the National Security Adviser, Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency, Director-General of the Department of State Services, and Director-General of the Defence Intelligence Agency to provide an immediate briefing on the allegations surrounding USAID’s funding of Boko Haram in Nigeria. We must get to the bottom of this matter, and I expect a thorough and transparent briefing from our national security leadership,” he said.

a6236.speaker: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) equality impact assessment
a6236.name: UK Foreign
a6236.title: Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) equality impact assessment
a6236.speech: Fears that slashing aid spending will likely see global deaths rise.

a6236.speaker: Rebecca Fabrizi, acting UK High Commissioner to Malawi
a6236.name: Rebecca Fabrizi
a6236.title: acting UK High Commissioner to Malawi
a6236.speech: Said in an email response that the UK's global Official Development Assistance (ODA) programme budget will be £8.7 billion in 2025/26, compared to £9.3 billion in 2024/25, and that the gradual reduction allows the UK to focus on priorities of tackling humanitarian, health and climate crises, underpinned by economic development, and to exit programmes responsibly over the course of the coming year ; “Ministers are conducting a line-by-line strategic review of our ODA programming, including our spend in countries like Malawi. The UK is a responsible aid partner and we will discuss changes with the Government of Malawi in due course. The UK remains committed to playing a significant role in international development as the Government implements its modernised approach to development.”

a6236.speaker: Maziko Matemba, chairperson of the International Coalition on Health Financing Advocacy
a6236.name: Maziko Matemba
a6236.title: chairperson of the International Coalition on Health Financing Advocacy
a6236.speech: Said for Malawi, where over 55 percent of total health expenditure comes from donors, such aid cuts spelt doom; said the UK, whose support towards health in Malawi was at 26 percent, focused more on sexual and reproductive health services while the US government concentrated on HIV and other programmes ; “The UK government has also been providing support to major donors for Malawi like the Global Fund and Gavi Vaccine Alliance. While funding is still being channelled to these institutions, it is also facing cuts. This cut will, thus, affect provision of vaccines, but also essential commodities like family planning. We need to invest in communities to ensure that we prevent more diseases from occurring.”

a6236.speaker: Norah Mwase, health financing specialist and economics lecturer at the University of Malawi
a6236.name: Norah Mwase
a6236.title: health financing specialist and economics lecturer at the University of Malawi
a6236.speech: Said the planned reduction in UK aid combined with ongoing cuts from USAid will create an aggregate shortfall of roughly £150 million for Malawi ; “Stock-outs of essential medicines are projected to increase in the next six months. Suspension or scaling down of community-based interventions is expected. Delays in procurement and maintenance of medical equipment, affecting over 30 district hospitals that rely on donor-funded capital investments, are inevitable.”

a6236.speaker: Norah Mwase, health financing specialist and economics lecturer at the University of Malawi
a6236.name: Norah Mwase
a6236.title: health financing specialist and economics lecturer at the University of Malawi
a6236.speech: Called for a steering committee, which includes representatives from the ministries of Health and Finance, civil society, and development partners to oversee resource mobilisation and ensure alignment with health priorities, and suggested: “Implement targeted ‘sin taxes’ on tobacco and alcohol, which could generate an additional £20 million annually for health. One percent levy on mobile money transactions could generate up to £10 million per year.”

a6236.speaker: George Jobe, Universal Health Coverage Coalition chairperson
a6236.name: George Jobe
a6236.title: Universal Health Coverage Coalition chairperson
a6236.speech: Urged several taxes towards health, including a percentage from toll-gates and carbon tax and health contribution fee on fizzy drinks.

a6236.speaker: Adrian Chikumbe, Ministry of Health spokesperson
a6236.name: Adrian Chikumbe
a6236.title: Ministry of Health spokesperson
a6236.speech: Was yet to respond by press time.

a6288.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6288.title: Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.speech: Writes that the Covid-19 pandemic has caused huge economic devastation to both individuals and businesses which ultimately resulted in the decline of economic activities and loss of income and jobs, and that it is therefore very important to take pride in supporting local businesses including Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) that have over the years faced stumbling blocks in accessing markets for their products; good lessons have been drawn from Covid-19, that it is very critical to be self-sufficient in case there is a shortage of imported products due to global calamities.

a6288.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6288.title: Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.speech: States that the Buy Local-Grow Namibia campaign was coined by the Ministry of Industrialisation and Trade to stimulate local consumption of goods and services, create awareness on consuming locally manufactured goods and educate consumers about the economic and social advantages local businesses bring; that Phase I focused on retailers, with some major retailers increasing their local sourcing by up to 40%, and Phase II focuses on sensitising local producers, manufacturers and entrepreneurs on branding and certification of their products to meet shelving standards as well as access to finance.

a6288.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6288.title: Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.speech: Notes that the local market is dominated by foreign imported goods and that local producers find it difficult to access retail shelf space because of challenges such as quality standards, access to finance and distribution channels, and that the ministry has continued to advocate for “Growth at Home” and has launched Namibia's own barcode to ease the identification of local products in the local and global marketplace.

a6288.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6288.title: Namibian Minister of Industrialisation and Trade (foreword)
a6288.speech: “I call on each and every Namibian to support this campaign through local purchases of our locally made products. I, therefore, wish to re-emphasise the ultimate goal of the Buy Namibia campaign, which is mainly to create a thriving local economy by maximising the potential of local businesses and increasing their market share and most importantly, creating the environment for Namibia to become a self-sustaining economy.”

a6480.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6480.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6480.speech: Has said it will need to drastically cut rations to refugees in Kenya due to reductions in global aid, including major funding cuts from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID).

a6480.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a6480.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)
a6480.speech: The two camps host nearly 800,000 people fleeing conflict and drought in Somalia and South Sudan, according to UNHCR.

a6480.speaker: Baimankay Sankoh, WFP’s deputy country director in Kenya
a6480.name: Baimankay Sankoh
a6480.title: WFP’s deputy country director in Kenya
a6480.speech: “WFP’s operations supporting refugees in Kenya are under immense strain” ; “With available resources stretched to their limits, we have had to make the difficult decision to again reduce food assistance. This will have a serious impact on vulnerable refugees, increasing the risk of hunger and malnutrition.”

a6480.speaker: Catherine Soi, Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Kakuma
a6480.name: Catherine Soi
a6480.title: Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Kakuma
a6480.speech: “There has been a lot of tension in the last couple of weeks or so” ; “People were very angry about what WFP is calling the priority food distribution, where some people will not get food at all and others are going to get a small fraction of the food.” ; said these tensions boiled over, triggering protests last week, which left one person dead and several others injured.

a6480.speaker: WFP officials (anonymous, spoke to Al Jazeera)
a6480.name: WFP officials (anonymous
a6480.title: spoke to Al Jazeera)
a6480.speech: Said the aid cuts from organisations like USAID meant they have had to make “very difficult decisions about who gets to eat and who doesn’t.”

a6480.speaker: Thomas Chica, WFP worker
a6480.name: Thomas Chica
a6480.title: WFP worker
a6480.speech: Explained that the new system was rolled out after assessments were conducted by WFP and its partners, and that refugees are now assessed based on their needs, rather than their status: “We need to look at them separately and differently and see how best we can channel the system so that it provides.” ; “Already the food that is being issued is quite low, 40 percent of the recommended ration, and this is being shared by a bigger chunk of the population,” adding that stocks will therefore not last as long as hoped; said that with its current resources dating from last year, WFP will only be able to provide assistance until December or January.

a6480.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6480.name: World Food Programme (WFP)
a6480.speech: Said in May that $44m was required to provide full rations and restore cash assistance for all refugees just through August.

a6794.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a6794.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a6794.title: Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a6794.speech: Highlighted that Namibia has been battling the HIV and AIDS epidemic for about 37 years now, since the first case of HIV was detected in 1986 ; “Based on the latest spectrum estimates, Namibia has achieved 92%–99%–94% of the UNAIDS 95–95–95 target. Meaning: Among the estimated PLHIV, 92% are aware of their HIV status. Among PLHIV who are aware of their HIV status, 99% are on ART. Among PLHIV on ART, 94% are virally suppressed. In summary, Namibia has surpassed the second 95% target and is close to achieving the first and third 95% targets. Congratulations, Namibia!”

a6794.speaker: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula, Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a6794.name: Dr. Kalumbi Shangula
a6794.title: Minister of Health and Social Services (Namibia)
a6794.speech: Stressed that the fight is not yet over and that the aim is to end AIDS as a Public Health Threat by 2030 ; “The Ministry has recently completed the review of the National Strategic Framework (NSF) for HIV/AIDS, interrogated data, and had conversations with all stakeholders up to the community level to understand how far we have gone in the response and also to get a better understanding of who is left behind in this response. As a result, a new National Strategic Framework for 2023-2024 to 2027-2028 is finalized and will be launched soon.”

a6961.speaker: Maj. David Kasimiro, Nimule Police Inspector
a6961.name: Maj. David Kasimiro
a6961.title: Nimule Police Inspector
a6961.speech: Said the truck transporting "untanned leather" to Uganda tumbled sideways due to poor road conditions and excessive weight of its cargo; confirmed that three men died at the scene while two others sustained injuries at around 5:00 PM, and that the truck driver has been arrested and is under investigation. "The truck loaded with untanned leather was traveling from Juba to Uganda. When it reached the checkpoint, due to poor road conditions and the truck being overloaded, it overturned and crushed five people." ; "All the victims were men—three died, and two were injured. The driver was not injured but has been arrested for investigation. The problem was the road conditions."

a6961.speaker: Dr. David Nyuma, Nimule Hospital Director
a6961.name: Dr. David Nyuma
a6961.title: Nimule Hospital Director
a6961.speech: Confirmed that the facility received two bodies, with a third person dying shortly after arrival: "We received three individuals—two were already dead, and the third passed away shortly after arrival. If there were other victims, they may not have come to the hospital."

a6961.speaker: Major Elijah Bill, traffic police officer
a6961.name: Major Elijah Bill
a6961.title: traffic police officer
a6961.speech: Confirmed that one of the victims was Sergeant Major Ngor Ajak, a customs officer, and added that the two survivors are in stable condition. "The leather load was quite heavy for the vehicle, causing it to fall and hit three people. One of the victims lost an arm and a leg and later succumbed to his injuries after being rushed to the hospital." ; "Two others were at the roadside, including Sergeant Major Ngor Ajak from the customs division, who also died. The accident left three dead, and two others sustained severe pain and minor."

a7002.speaker: Nigerian House of Representatives
a7002.name: Nigerian House of Representatives
a7002.speech: Set up a Special Committee to conduct a thorough investigation into allegations made by U.S. Congressman Scott Perry; urged the Federal Government to engage with the U.S. Government through its Committee on Foreign Affairs to obtain a formal clarification on the matter; mandated its Committees on National Security and Intelligence, Defence, Foreign Affairs, and Inter-Governmental Affairs to investigate the activities of NGOs operating in Nigeria, their identities, sources of funding, and how their funds are utilized; called on the media and the general public to remain vigilant and provide relevant information to assist security agencies in combating terrorism ; expressed concern that leaving the allegation uninvestigated could undermine Nigeria's sovereignty, compromise national security efforts, and erode public confidence in the country's fight against terrorism.

a7002.speaker: Scott Perry, U.S. Congressman
a7002.name: Scott Perry
a7002.title: U.S. Congressman
a7002.speech: Claimed that USAID had been involved in funding Boko Haram and other terrorist groups operating in various countries, alleging during the inaugural hearing of the U.S. House Subcommittee on Delivering on Government Efficiency that "$697 million (was spent) annually, plus shipments of cash funds in Madrasas, ISIS, Al-Qaeda, Boko Haram," among others.

a7002.speaker: Hon. Inuwa Garba, Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Engineering, representing Yamaltu-Deba Federal Constituency, Gombe State
a7002.name: Hon. Inuwa Garba
a7002.title: Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Engineering, representing Yamaltu-Deba Federal Constituency, Gombe State
a7002.speech: In his motion, expressed grave concern over Congressman Scott Perry's recent claim; emphasized that, given Boko Haram's dominant presence in northern Nigeria, it is reasonable to assume that the group may have significantly benefited from this alleged funding. "If true, this allegation raises serious national and international security concerns, particularly regarding external influences on Nigeria's fight against insurgency and terrorism," he said ; he further highlighted that Nigeria has battled terrorism for over a decade, committing substantial resources to counterterrorism operations while seeking international cooperation, and that the crisis has resulted in significant loss of lives, destruction of property, and the displacement of over one million citizens ; addressing journalists after plenary, he described the allegations as "deeply troubling and warranting a thorough investigation."

a7002.speaker: Hon. Inuwa Garba, Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Engineering
a7002.name: Hon. Inuwa Garba
a7002.title: Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Engineering
a7002.speech: Cited statistics indicating that USAID had spent approximately $2.7 billion in Nigeria between 2022 and 2024. "However, to our dismay, this expenditure did not meet our expectations," he stated; while acknowledging that the allegations remain unverified, he stressed that they cast a shadow over USAID, an agency purportedly dedicated to humanitarian assistance.

a7002.speaker: Hon. Inuwa Garba, Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Engineering
a7002.name: Hon. Inuwa Garba
a7002.title: Chairman of the House Committee on Science and Engineering
a7002.speech: Expressed confidence in the House Committee on NGOs, led by Hon. Victor Uguzor, to conduct a comprehensive investigation, emphasizing the need to verify the claim: "If true, this allegation raises grave national and international security concerns, particularly regarding external influences on Nigeria's fight against insecurity. Over the years, this crisis has resulted in significant loss of lives, widespread destruction of property, and the displacement of more than one million citizens."

a7016.speaker: Iara Lee, Brazilian filmmaker of Korean origin
a7016.name: Iara Lee
a7016.title: Brazilian filmmaker of Korean origin
a7016.speech: Says that, with the events of the 11th, her concern became sending humanitarian aid and helping the people in São Vicente rather than screening her film ; “Especially because they had to cancel the screening in August, but they asked me to come back in September; that will not be possible, I will have to return to Brazil. I was coming for three months, but a scalding with hot water on part of my body, a third-degree burn, forces me to change my plans, unfortunately.”

a7016.speaker: Iara Lee, Brazilian filmmaker of Korean origin
a7016.name: Iara Lee
a7016.title: Brazilian filmmaker of Korean origin
a7016.speech: “I have a prize called the Creative Activism Award, worth 1,000 dollars, which aims to reward people who use creativity to overcome obstacles by every means: recycling, biology, dance, photography, dance, poetry, whatever one can imagine to turn trash into treasure, to turn negatives into positives. Around 300 people and groups have already received this prize,” explains Iara Lee.

a7016.speaker: Iara Lee, Brazilian filmmaker of Korean origin
a7016.name: Iara Lee
a7016.title: Brazilian filmmaker of Korean origin
a7016.speech: “I offered them a drone so they could better monitor the sea turtles; there are other groups that work with underprivileged children, and we also gave them materials, as well as to the fish markets of Sal. I learned that they are going to screen my film about the women of Guinea-Bissau there, about agro-ecology.”

a7046.speaker: Nigel Green, CEO of deVere Group
a7046.name: Nigel Green
a7046.title: CEO of deVere Group
a7046.speech: Issued a stark warning that a swift retaliation from Europe would likely deliver a hammer blow to US stocks. He said: “While market analysts are closely tracking the slide in European stocks impacted by the prospect of new US tariffs should Trump win the presidency, we’re issuing a crucial warning that’s been largely overlooked: American companies with substantial European sales may be next in line for a hit. As Donald Trump’s odds of winning the US presidential election improve, we believe the market is underestimating the risk of swift European retaliation and the pressure this could place on key American stocks. If Trump returns to the White House and reinitiates his hardline trade policies, Europe is likely to respond in kind, creating a significant downside risk for US companies with exposure to European markets. This includes leading firms across sectors from tech and consumer goods to luxury and automotive, which could see profits squeezed by tariffs and changing market dynamics. Many of these companies, which rely heavily on revenue from Europe, are still trading at robust valuations—a vulnerability that may soon be exposed.” ; He continued: “Investors need to consider the very real possibility of a new trade conflict between the US and Europe. While much of the focus has been on European stocks with exposure to US markets, the impact on American companies with significant European sales has largely been ignored. This is a clear blind spot that we’re urging investors to take seriously.” ; Green concluded: “As Trump’s White House chances seem to approve, we’re sounding the alarm on US firms with heavy European ties and market dominance as retaliation is likely to be swift.”

a7046.speaker: Barclays (basket of European stocks exposed to US tariffs)
a7046.name: Barclays (basket of European stocks exposed to US tariffs)
a7046.speech: A basket of 28 European stocks exposed to US tariffs compiled by Barclays has tumbled 7% since late September as the former president’s odds of an election victory shorten.

a7058.speaker: Laouli Labo, Secretary General of Niger’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad
a7058.name: Laouli Labo
a7058.title: Secretary General of Niger’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad
a7058.speech: Said the process falls “within the continuation of the consultations organised in June 2022, and of the intergovernmental negotiations scheduled for November 2023, which all fall within the framework of strengthening this cooperation” ; Recalled that “Niger-German development cooperation is the fruit of a close collaboration forged between the Government of the Republic of Niger and the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany, right after Niger’s independence, with the signing of the first Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement on 14 June 1961 in Niamey” ; Said “the regular holding of intergovernmental consultations between our two countries, the high-level visits and the cumulative contributions of this cooperation over the years, estimated at nearly 800 billion CFA francs, eloquently testify to the quality and vitality of our relations” ; Stressed that “following the brief suspension of this cooperation as a consequence of the events of 26 July 2023 in Niger, the Federal Republic of Germany, in the following months, began to soften its reading of the situation and entered into dialogue with the new authorities with a view to a better understanding and a resumption of cooperation activities, which are reputed to be essentially centred on the populations and on priority sectors such as agriculture, livestock, education and training, health, climate and the environment, and decentralisation” ; Indicated that at the conclusion of the consultations “we are expected to take stock of the projects and actions implemented by Germany in Niger through our various ministerial departments and our structures, to identify the obstacles that limit its ambitions and to map out prospects favourable to the revitalisation of this North-South cooperation, which is already exemplary” ; “This will also be an opportunity for us to agree on future commitments and new orientations in order better to prepare the future intergovernmental negotiations,” he continued, reaffirming his conviction that “the results of these consultations will be such as to further consolidate the relations between our two countries”.

a7058.speaker: Dr. Oliver Schnakenberg, Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to Niger
a7058.name: Dr. Oliver Schnakenberg
a7058.title: Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to Niger
a7058.speech: Stressed that the organisation of this meeting “testifies to the importance we jointly attach to the quality of our partnership, and this day represents a new phase in our bilateral cooperation” ; Said that despite the temporary and partial suspension of bilateral cooperation after the events of 26 July 2023, “this never meant that we had abandoned Niger”, adding that they “provided direct humanitarian aid without interruption and we have remained one of the main donors of the United Nations nutrition and health programmes in Niger” ; Explained that they were gathered to talk about the revitalisation of their partnership because their partner remains “the Nigerien people and nation and not certain representatives who come and go” ; Commended the people and authorities of Niger for the holding of the national consultations that led to the charter of refoundation, which constitutes “an act of national self-determination”.

a7058.speaker: Dr. Bernhard Braune, head of the German delegation
a7058.name: Dr. Bernhard Braune
a7058.title: head of the German delegation
a7058.speech: Explained that this bilateral meeting “testifies to our shared commitment to sustainable development and shared prosperity, and cooperation between our two countries began shortly after Niger’s independence in the early 1960s. For more than six decades, it has established itself as a solid, sincere, resilient partnership, deeply rooted in the needs of the populations” ; Expressed, on behalf of the Federal Republic of Germany, his solidarity with the people of Niger in particular and of the Sahel in general in the face of the challenges they face, notably those of a security nature, while reaffirming their commitment to strengthening their cooperation.

a7349.speaker: Nana Professor Oheneba Boakye Adjei Owoahene, Otumfuo’s Hiahene and Chairman of the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II (OOTII) foundation
a7349.name: Nana Professor Oheneba Boakye Adjei Owoahene
a7349.title: Otumfuo’s Hiahene and Chairman of the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II (OOTII) foundation
a7349.speech: noted that Breast Care International (BCI), with the collaboration effort from the Global Health Catalyst Summit, USA and the Otumfuo Osei Tutu II foundation, has taken the bold initiative to establish a Comprehensive Cancer Centre of Excellence (CCCOE) at an estimated cost of $100 million ; He said the Comprehensive Cancer Centre of Excellence (CCCOE), to be built in phases, would provide the much-needed dedicated facility for cancer care, prevention, awareness creation, diagnostics, screening, treatment, research, training, education, telemedicine, AI Hub, palliative care and rehabilitation including survivorship, for all cancers.

a7349.speaker: Dr. (Mrs.) Beatrice Wiafe Addai, Chief Executive Officer of Peace and Love Hospitals and President and Founder of Breast Care International (BCI)
a7349.name: Dr. (Mrs.) Beatrice Wiafe Addai
a7349.title: Chief Executive Officer of Peace and Love Hospitals and President and Founder of Breast Care International (BCI)
a7349.speech: said Ghana, like many other developing nations, faced a rising incidence of cancer, placing a severe strain on existing healthcare infrastructures ; bemoaned the lack of a dedicated facility for cancer education, prevention, screening diagnosis, treatment, training and research ; noted that challenges faced by patients and healthcare professionals became a compelling case for the establishment of a stand-alone comprehensive cancer centre of excellence to address the growing burden of the disease.

a7418.speaker: Manoma Vusie Masango, National Commissioner of Police, Royal Eswatini Police Service
a7418.name: Manoma Vusie Masango
a7418.title: National Commissioner of Police, Royal Eswatini Police Service
a7418.speech: Called on 32 Individual Police Officers from the Royal Eswatini Police Service to embody discipline, honour, and respect for human rights as they prepare to join the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission (AUSSOM) in Mogadishu, Somalia ; reminded the officers that their role is not only to represent Eswatini but also to safeguard civilians and uphold international law in a conflict-torn region ; “You have reflected an earnest intention on the commitment of member states to the contribution of peace and security in the continent.” ; “Go with purpose, humility, and the unwavering determination to serve the African people. Your safety, conduct, and discipline will remain our highest priority and concern.” ; emphasized the importance of adhering to International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Human Rights Law (IHRL) while on mission, stressing that the officers must protect civilians and respect the Rule of Law in line with the principles of African Union Peace Support Operations.

a7418.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a7418.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a7418.speech: According to OCHA, over 6.9 million Somalis currently need humanitarian assistance due to conflict, drought, and food insecurity.

a7418.speaker: The African Union and its international partners, including the United Nations and the European Union
a7418.name: The African Union and its international partners
a7418.title: including the United Nations and the European Union
a7418.speech: Have repeatedly stressed that instability in Somalia is a continental concern.

a7418.speaker: African Union
a7418.name: African Union
a7418.speech: Has committed to a gradual transfer of security responsibilities to Somali authorities, with the ultimate goal of allowing Somalia to take full ownership of its peace and security.
